title.en: Volume 105 Biographies 43: Cheng Cai, Ren Xiongxiang, Kong Fan Son: Zheng, Fan Gong, Zhang Yongzhi, Liu Shu, Wang Shu, Yang Boxiong Cousin: Boyuan, Xiao Gong, Wendihandida, Zhang Han, Ren Tianchong
title.raw: 卷一百〇五 列傳第四十三: 程寀 任熊祥 孔璠子:拯 范拱 張用直 劉樞 王翛 楊伯雄族兄:伯淵 蕭貢 溫蒂罕締達 張翰 任天寵 Volume 105 Biographies 43: Cheng Cai, Ren Xiongxiang, Kong Fan Son: Zheng, Fan Gong, Zhang Yongzhi, Liu Shu, Wang Shu, Yang Boxiong Cousin: Boyuan, Xiao Gong, Wendihandida, Zhang Han, Ren Tianchong

sentences.zh: 程寀，字公弼，燕之析津人。

translations.literal: Cheng Cai, courtesy name Gongbi, was a native of Xijin in Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Cai, whose style name was Gongbi, came from Xijin in the Yan region.

sentences.zh: 祖冀，仕遼廣德軍節度使。

translations.literal: His grandfather Ji served as military governor of the Guangde Army under the Liao.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Ji had served as military governor of the Guangde Army in Liao service.

sentences.zh: 冀凡六男，父子皆擢科第，士族號其家為「程一舉」。

translations.literal: Ji had six sons in all; father and sons all passed the civil examinations, and the gentry styled their household "One Examination Cheng."
translations.idiomatic: Ji had six sons altogether, and father and sons alike won places on the civil examinations, so the literati nicknamed the household "the Chengs who pass in one sitting."

sentences.zh: 冀次子四穆，遼崇義軍節度使。

translations.literal: Ji's second son Simu was military governor of the Chongyi Army under the Liao.
translations.idiomatic: Ji's second son, Simu, served as military governor of the Chongyi Army under the Liao.

sentences.zh: 寀，四穆之季子也。

translations.literal: Cai was the youngest son of Simu.
translations.idiomatic: Cai was Simu's youngest son.

sentences.zh: 自幼如成人。

translations.literal: From childhood he was like an adult.
translations.idiomatic: Even as a child he conducted himself like a grown man.

sentences.zh: 及冠，篤學，中進士甲科，累遷殿中丞。

translations.literal: Upon reaching manhood he studied earnestly, passed the jinshi examination in the top class, and was repeatedly promoted to Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: When he came of age he devoted himself to learning, placed in the highest class of the jinshi examination, and rose through successive appointments to Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 天輔七年，太祖入燕，授尚書都官員外郎、錦州安昌令，累加起居郎，為史館修撰，以從軍有勞，加少府少監。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Tianfu, when the Taizu entered Yan, he was appointed Vice Director of the Bureau of Punishments in the Ministry of Works and magistrate of Anchang in Jinzhou; he was successively promoted to Attendant of the Heir Apparent, served as compiler in the Historiography Institute, and for meritorious service on campaign was made Vice Director of the Palace Workshops.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Tianfu, after Taizu took Yan, he received appointment as vice director of punishments in the Ministry of Works and as magistrate of Anchang in Jinzhou; he was later made attendant of the heir apparent and compiler at the Historiography Institute, and for distinguished service on campaign was promoted to vice director of the palace workshops.

sentences.zh: 熙宗時，曆翰林待制，兼右諫議大夫。

translations.literal: Under Emperor Xizong he served as Hanlin academician awaiting orders and concurrently as Right Remonstrating Grand Master.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Xizong he held posts as Hanlin academician awaiting orders and as right remonstrating grand master at the same time.

sentences.zh: 寀上疏言事，其略曰：「殿前點檢司，古殿岩環衛之任，所以肅禁禦，尊天子、備不虞也。

translations.literal: Cai submitted a memorial on state affairs, the gist of which read: "The Palace Front Inspection Office bears the ancient duty of guarding the imperial precincts, to enforce the inner prohibitions, honor the Son of Heaven, and guard against the unforeseen.
translations.idiomatic: Cai submitted a memorial on affairs of state, which in summary said: "The Palace Front Inspection Office carries the ancient charge of guarding the imperial precincts—to enforce the inner prohibitions, honor the Son of Heaven, and guard against the unforeseen.

sentences.zh: 臣幸得近清光，從天子觀時畋之禮。

translations.literal: Your subject has been fortunate to draw near the clear radiance and follow the Son of Heaven in observing the seasonal hunt.
translations.idiomatic: I have had the good fortune to stand near Your Majesty and accompany you in observing the seasonal hunt.

sentences.zh: 比見陛下校獵，凡羽衛從臣，無貴賤皆得執弓矢馳逐，而聖駕崎嶇沙礫之地，加之林木叢郁，易以迷失。

translations.literal: Recently I have seen Your Majesty on the training hunt: all guards and attendant officials, without distinction of rank, were allowed to take bow and arrow and gallop in pursuit, while the imperial carriage was in rugged ground of sand and gravel, and moreover in dense woodland, where one could easily lose the way.
translations.idiomatic: Recently, when Your Majesty went on a training hunt, every guard and attendant official, high or low, was allowed to take up bow and arrow and ride in pursuit, while the imperial carriage was on rough ground of sand and gravel amid thick woodland where one could easily lose the way.

sentences.zh: 是日自卯及申，百官始出沙漠，獨不知車駕何在。

translations.literal: That day from the hour mao until shen the officials only emerged from the desert, yet alone did not know where the imperial carriage was.
translations.idiomatic: That day, from early morning until mid-afternoon, the officials at last came out of the desert still not knowing where the imperial carriage was.

sentences.zh: 瞻望久之，始有騎來報，皇帝從數騎已至行在。

translations.literal: After gazing long, at last a rider came to report that the emperor with a few horsemen had already reached the temporary palace.
translations.idiomatic: After a long wait, a rider at last arrived to report that the emperor, with only a few horsemen, had already reached the temporary encampment.

sentences.zh: 竊惟古天子出入警蹕，清道而行。

translations.literal: I venture to consider that in antiquity when the Son of Heaven went out or in, there were warnings and halts, and the road was cleared before he traveled.
translations.idiomatic: I reflect that in antiquity, whenever the Son of Heaven went abroad, the route was cleared and guarded with warnings and halts.

sentences.zh: 至於楚畋雲夢，漢獵長楊，皆大陳兵衛，以備非常。

translations.literal: As for the Chu hunt in Yunmeng and the Han hunt at Changyang, all greatly arrayed military guards to guard against the unforeseen.
translations.idiomatic: When the Chu hunted in Yunmeng or the Han at Changyang, they all deployed large military escorts against the unforeseen.

sentences.zh: 陛下膺祖宗付託之重，奈何獨與數騎出入林麓沙漠之中，前無斥候，後無羽衛，甚非肅禁禦之意也。

translations.literal: Your Majesty bears the heavy trust the ancestors have handed down—how can you go alone with a few horsemen into forests, hills, and desert, with no scouts ahead and no guards behind? This is very far from the intent of enforcing the inner prohibitions.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty bears the weighty trust your ancestors placed in you—how can you ride out alone with only a few horsemen into forest, hill, and desert, with no scouts ahead and no guards behind? That falls far short of what enforcing the inner prohibitions requires.

sentences.zh: 臣願陛下熟計之。

translations.literal: Your subject wishes Your Majesty to consider this carefully.
translations.idiomatic: I urge Your Majesty to weigh this matter carefully.

sentences.zh: 後若複獵，當預戒有司，圖上獵地，具其可否，然後下令清道而行。

translations.literal: If Your Majesty hunts again hereafter, you should beforehand warn the responsible offices, map the hunting grounds, set forth what is feasible or not, and only then order the road cleared for travel.
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty hunts again, you should first instruct the responsible offices to map the hunting grounds and report what is feasible, and only then order the route cleared.

sentences.zh: 擇沖要稍平之地，為駐蹕之所，簡忠義爪牙之士，統以親信腹心之臣，警衛左右。

translations.literal: Choose a strategic place somewhat level as the site where the carriage halts; select loyal and resolute warriors; place them under trusted ministers who are close to the heart; and guard left and right.
translations.idiomatic: Choose a level spot at a strategic point for the halt of the imperial carriage, select loyal and resolute warriors, place them under trusted inner ministers, and post them as guards on either side.

sentences.zh: 俟其麋鹿既來，然後馳射。

translations.literal: Wait until the deer have come, and only then gallop forth to shoot.
translations.idiomatic: Wait until the deer have gathered, and only then ride out to shoot.

sentences.zh: 仍先遣搜閱林藪，明立標幟，為出入之馳道。

translations.literal: Moreover, first send men to search the woods and thickets, clearly set up markers, and make galloping lanes for going out and in.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, send men ahead to search the woods and thickets, set up clear markers, and lay out riding lanes for entry and exit.

sentences.zh: 不然，後恐貽宗朝社稷之憂。」

translations.literal: Otherwise, hereafter I fear it may bring worry upon the ancestral court and the altars of soil and grain."
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise, I fear the ancestral court and the altars of state may yet suffer for it."

sentences.zh: 又曰：「臣伏讀唐史，追尊高祖以下，諡號或加至十八字。

translations.literal: He also said: "Your subject has read the Tang histories in reverence: in posthumous elevation from Gaozu downward, posthumous titles were sometimes extended to eighteen characters.
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote: "Having studied the Tang histories, I find that in posthumous honors from Gaozu onward, epithets were sometimes extended to as many as eighteen characters.

sentences.zh: 前宋大中祥符間亦加至十六字，亡遼因之，近陛下亦受'崇天體道欽明文武聖德'十字。

translations.literal: In the former Song, during the Dazhong Xiangfu era, titles were also extended to sixteen characters; the fallen Liao followed this, and recently Your Majesty also received the ten characters 'Revering Heaven, Embodying the Way, Respectful and Bright in Civil and Military Sagely Virtue.'
translations.idiomatic: Under the former Song, in the Dazhong Xiangfu period, epithets likewise reached sixteen characters; the fallen Liao followed suit, and recently Your Majesty received the ten-character style 'Revering Heaven, Embodying the Way, Respectful and Bright in Civil and Military Sagely Virtue.'

sentences.zh: 臣竊謂人臣以歸美報上為忠，天子以追崇祖考為孝。

translations.literal: Your subject ventures to say that for a minister to return beauty and repay the sovereign is loyalty, and for the Son of Heaven to pursue honor for ancestors and father is filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: I would say that when ministers return praise to their ruler they show loyalty, and when the Son of Heaven honors his forebears he shows filial piety.

sentences.zh: 太祖武元皇帝受命開基，八年之間，奄有天下，功德茂盛，振古無前，止諡'武元'二字，理或未安，何以示將來？

translations.literal: Taizu the Martial Yuan Emperor received the Mandate and founded the dynasty; within eight years he suddenly possessed the realm. His merit and virtue were luxuriant, unmatched since antiquity—yet he bears only the two-character posthumous title 'Martial Yuan.' Reason may find this not yet settled; how is this to be shown to posterity?
translations.idiomatic: Taizu the Martial Yuan Emperor received the Mandate and founded the dynasty; within eight years he held the realm. His achievements were abundant and without parallel in history—yet he bears only the two-character epithet Martial Yuan. That may not yet be fitting; what lesson does that teach posterity?

sentences.zh: 臣願詔有司定議諡號，庶幾上慰祖宗在天之靈，使耿光丕烈，傳於無窮。」

translations.literal: Your subject wishes Your Majesty to decree that the responsible offices deliberate and fix a posthumous title, so that above you may comfort the spirits of the ancestors in Heaven and make their bright glory and great deeds transmitted without end."
translations.idiomatic: I urge Your Majesty to order the responsible offices to deliberate and fix a posthumous title, so that the spirits of your ancestors in Heaven may be comforted and their bright glory and great deeds handed down forever."

sentences.zh: 又曰：「古者天子皆有巡狩，無非事者。

translations.literal: He also said: "In antiquity the Son of Heaven always had inspection tours, and none were without purpose.
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote: "In antiquity every Son of Heaven made inspection tours, and none were idle excursions.

sentences.zh: 或省察風俗，或審理冤獄，或問民疾苦，以布宣德澤，皆巡狩之名也。

translations.literal: Some inspected customs, some reviewed unjust cases, some inquired into the people's hardships, to spread and proclaim virtuous favor—all were in the name of inspection tours.
translations.idiomatic: Some inspected local customs, some reviewed unjust cases, some inquired into popular hardship, spreading virtuous favor in the name of the inspection tour.

sentences.zh: 國家肇興，誠恐郡國新民，逐末棄本，習舊染之汙，奢侈詐偽，或有不明之獄，僭濫之刑，或力役無時，四民失業。

translations.literal: Since the state first arose, I truly fear that in the commanderies and districts the new people may pursue the secondary and abandon the root, practice the stains of old habits, be extravagant and deceitful, or there may be unclear cases, excessive punishments, or corvée labor without season so that the four classes lose their livelihoods.
translations.idiomatic: Since the dynasty was founded, I truly fear that in the provinces the new subjects may chase profit and abandon the fundamentals, cling to old corruptions, grow extravagant and deceitful, leave cases unclear, impose punishments beyond measure, or demand labor without regard to season so that the four classes lose their livelihood.

sentences.zh: 今鑾輅省方，將憲古行事，臣願天心洞照，委之長貳，厘正風俗，或置匭匣，以申冤枉，或遣使郡國，問民無告，皆古巡狩之事。

translations.literal: Now the imperial carriage inspects the regions and will take the ancients as law in action. Your subject wishes that Heaven's heart may shine through clearly: entrust it to the chief deputies, rectify customs, or set up complaint boxes to voice wrongs, or send envoys to the commanderies and districts to ask after those with no one to plead for them—all are matters of the ancient inspection tours.
translations.idiomatic: Now that the imperial carriage is touring the realm and will act as the ancients did, I pray that Heaven's favor may shine through: entrust the work to your chief deputies to rectify customs, set up complaint boxes for the wronged, or send envoys through the provinces to hear those with no advocate—all duties of the ancient inspection tour.

sentences.zh: 昔漢昭帝問疾苦，光武求民瘼，如此則和氣通，天下丕平可坐而待也。」

translations.literal: Formerly Emperor Zhao of Han inquired into hardships, and Emperor Guangwu of Han sought the people's afflictions; if it is thus, harmonizing qi will penetrate and great peace under Heaven may be awaited while seated."
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhao of Han inquired into hardship and Emperor Guangwu sought the people's afflictions, harmony followed and great peace could be awaited at ease."

sentences.zh: 又曰：「臣聞，善醫者不視他人之肥瘠，察其脈之病否而已；

translations.literal: He also said: "Your subject has heard that a skilled physician does not look at another person's fatness or leanness but examines whether the pulse is diseased or not;
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote: "I have heard that a skilled physician does not judge by another's fat or thin frame but examines whether the pulse is sound;

sentences.zh: 善計天下者不視天下之安危，察其紀綱理否而已。

translations.literal: one who is skilled at reckoning the realm does not look at the realm's safety or danger but examines whether its statutes and guidelines are in order or not.
translations.idiomatic: and one skilled at governing the realm does not look at surface safety or danger but examines whether its institutions are in order.

sentences.zh: 天下者人也，安危者肥瘠也，紀綱者脈也，脈不病雖瘠不害，脈病而肥者危矣。

translations.literal: The realm is the person, safety and danger are fatness and leanness, statutes and guidelines are the pulse: if the pulse is not diseased, though lean it is not harmful; if the pulse is diseased, though fat one is in peril.
translations.idiomatic: The realm is the body, safety and danger are its fat or leanness, and statutes are the pulse: if the pulse is sound, leanness does no harm; if the pulse is diseased, even fatness is perilous.

sentences.zh: 是故，四肢雖無故，不足恃也，脈而已矣。

translations.literal: Therefore, though the four limbs are without ailment, they are not to be relied upon—only the pulse.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore, though the four limbs show no ailment, they cannot be trusted—only the pulse matters.

sentences.zh: 天下雖無事，不足矜也，綱紀而已矣。

translations.literal: Though the realm has no affairs, it is not to be prized—only the statutes and guidelines.
translations.idiomatic: Though the realm seems untroubled, that is no cause for pride—only the institutions matter.

sentences.zh: 尚書省，天子喉舌之官，綱紀在焉。

translations.literal: The Department of State Affairs is the Son of Heaven's organ of voice and tongue; the statutes and guidelines reside there.
translations.idiomatic: The Department of State Affairs is the Son of Heaven's voice; within it lie the institutions of governance.

sentences.zh: 臣願詔尚書省，戒勵百官，各揚其職，以立綱紀。

translations.literal: Your subject wishes Your Majesty to decree to the Department of State Affairs to admonish and encourage the hundred officials, each to display his duty, thereby to establish the statutes and guidelines.
translations.idiomatic: I urge Your Majesty to decree to the Department of State Affairs that it admonish and encourage every official to perform his duty and thereby establish sound institutions.

sentences.zh: 如吏部天官以進賢退不肖為任，誠使升黜有科，任得其人，則綱紀理而民受其賜，前代興替，未始不由此者。」

translations.literal: As the Ministry of Personnel, the celestial office, takes advancing the worthy and removing the unworthy as its charge—if promotion and demotion truly have standards and appointments gain the right men, then the statutes and guidelines are ordered and the people receive its blessing; the rise and fall of former ages never failed to stem from this."
translations.idiomatic: As the Ministry of Personnel, the celestial office, exists to advance the worthy and remove the unworthy—if promotion and demotion follow clear standards and the right men hold office, institutions will be sound and the people will benefit; the rise and fall of every former age has turned on this."

sentences.zh: 又曰：「虞舜不告而娶二妃。

translations.literal: He also said: "Yu Shun married two consorts without informing his parents.
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote: "Yu Shun took two consorts without informing his parents.

sentences.zh: 帝嚳娶四妃，法天之四星。

translations.literal: Emperor Ku took four consorts, modeling Heaven's four stars.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ku took four consorts, following the pattern of Heaven's four stars.

sentences.zh: 周文王一後、三夫人，嬪禦有數。

translations.literal: King Wen of Zhou had one queen and three ladies, and the ranks of consorts and attendants were fixed in number.
translations.idiomatic: King Wen of Zhou had one queen and three chief ladies, with fixed numbers for consorts and attendants.

sentences.zh: 選求淑媛以充後宮，帝王之制也。

translations.literal: Selecting and seeking virtuous ladies to fill the inner palace is the institution of emperors and kings.
translations.idiomatic: Choosing virtuous ladies to fill the inner palace is the established practice of kings and emperors.

sentences.zh: 然女無美惡，入宮見妒，陛下欲廣嗣續，不可不知而告戒之。」

translations.literal: Yet women, whether beautiful or not, once they enter the palace meet jealousy. Your Majesty wishes to extend the succession—you cannot fail to know this and instruct and warn them."
translations.idiomatic: Yet whether fair or plain, once a woman enters the palace she meets jealousy. If Your Majesty wishes to extend the succession, you must know this and instruct and warn them."

sentences.zh: 又曰：「臣伏見本朝富有四海，禮樂制度，莫不一新。

translations.literal: He also said: "Your subject has seen in reverence that this dynasty is rich in possessing the four seas; rites, music, and institutions are all newly made.
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote: "I observe that this dynasty holds the four seas and has renewed rites, music, and institutions throughout.

sentences.zh: 宮禁之制，尚未嚴密，胥吏健卒之輩，皆得出入，莫有呵止，至淆混而無別。

translations.literal: The regulations of the palace prohibitions are not yet strict: clerks, strong soldiers, and the like all may go in and out, and none halt or challenge them, until confusion mixes and there is no distinction.
translations.idiomatic: Palace security is not yet strict: clerks and strong soldiers alike come and go without challenge, until all distinction is lost in confusion.

sentences.zh: 雖有闌入之法，久尚未行，甚非嚴禁衛、明法令之意，陛下不可不知而必行。」

translations.literal: Although there are laws against unlawful entry, for long they have not been enforced—very far from the intent of strict inner prohibitions and clarifying statutes and orders. Your Majesty cannot fail to know this and must enforce it."
translations.idiomatic: Though laws against unlawful entry exist, they have long gone unenforced—far from the intent of strict palace guard and clear law. Your Majesty must know this and enforce it without fail."

sentences.zh: 疏奏，上嘉納之，於是始命有司議增上太祖尊諡。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted, the emperor praised and accepted it; thereupon he first ordered the responsible offices to deliberate on augmenting Taizu's honored posthumous title.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial was submitted, the emperor praised and accepted it, and then first ordered the responsible offices to deliberate on augmenting Taizu's posthumous honors.

sentences.zh: 皇統八年十二月，由翰林侍講學士為橫海軍節度使，移彰德軍節度使。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of the eighth year of Huangtong he went from Hanlin attendant lecturer to military governor of the Henghai Army, then was transferred to military governor of the Zhangde Army.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of the eighth year of Huangtong he moved from Hanlin attendant lecturer to military governor of the Henghai Army, and was later transferred to military governor of the Zhangde Army.

sentences.zh: 卒官，年六十二。

translations.literal: He died in office at the age of sixty-two.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office at the age of sixty-two.

sentences.zh: 寀剛直耿介，不諂奉權貴以希苟進，有古君子之風雲。

translations.literal: Cai was upright and high-principled; he did not flatter the powerful and noble to hope for careless advancement, and had the air of the gentlemen of old.
translations.idiomatic: Cai was upright and principled; he would not flatter the powerful for advancement, and bore the manner of the gentlemen of old.

sentences.zh: 任熊祥

translations.literal: Ren Xiongxiang
translations.idiomatic: Ren Xiongxiang

sentences.zh: 任熊祥，字子仁。

translations.literal: Ren Xiongxiang, courtesy name Ziren.
translations.idiomatic: Ren Xiongxiang, whose style name was Ziren.

sentences.zh: 八代祖圜，為後唐宰相。

translations.literal: His ancestor Yuan in the eighth generation was a chief minister of Later Tang.
translations.idiomatic: His ancestor Yuan, eight generations back, had been chief minister of Later Tang.

sentences.zh: 圜孫睿，隨石晉北遷，遂為燕人。

translations.literal: Yuan's grandson Rui followed the Later Jin north in migration and thus became a man of Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan's grandson Rui moved north with the Later Jin and thus became a native of Yan.

sentences.zh: 熊祥登遼天慶八年進士第，為樞密院令史。

translations.literal: Xiongxiang passed the jinshi examination in the eighth year of Liao Tianqing and served as clerk of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Xiongxiang passed the jinshi examination in the eighth year of Liao Tianqing and served as a clerk in the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 太祖平燕，以其地畀宋，熊祥至汴，授武當丞。

translations.literal: When Taizu pacified Yan and gave its territory to Song, Xiongxiang went to Bian and was appointed assistant magistrate of Wudang.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizu pacified Yan and ceded the region to Song, Xiongxiang went to Bian and was appointed assistant magistrate of Wudang.

sentences.zh: 宋法，新附官不厘務，熊祥言于郡守楊皙曰：「既不與事，請止給半俸以養親。」

translations.literal: By Song law, newly submitted officials did not take on duties. Xiongxiang said to the prefect Yang Xi: "Since I am not given affairs, I ask only to receive half salary to support my parents."
translations.idiomatic: Under Song law, newly submitted officials were not assigned duties. Xiongxiang told the prefect Yang Xi: "Since I am given no duties, I ask only for half salary to support my parents."

sentences.zh: 皙雖不許，而喜其廉。

translations.literal: Xi did not consent, yet was pleased at his integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Xi did not agree, but was pleased by his integrity.

sentences.zh: 金人取均、房州，熊祥歸朝，複為樞密院令史。

translations.literal: When the Jin took Jun and Fang prefectures, Xiongxiang returned to court and again became clerk of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jin took Jun and Fang prefectures, Xiongxiang returned to court and again served as a clerk in the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 時西京留守高慶裔攝院事，無敢忤其意者，熊祥未嘗阿意事之。

translations.literal: At that time Gao Qingyi, Western Capital regent, held acting charge of the bureau's affairs; none dared go against his intent, yet Xiongxiang never fawned on him in service.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Gao Qingyi, regent of the Western Capital, held acting charge of the bureau; no one dared cross him, yet Xiongxiang never curried favor with him.

sentences.zh: 其後杜充、劉筈同知燕京行省，法制未一，日有異論，熊祥為折衷之。

translations.literal: Afterward Du Chong and Liu Kuo were co-administrators of the Yanjing Branch Secretariat; laws and institutions were not unified, and each day there were differing opinions—Xiongxiang mediated and balanced them.
translations.idiomatic: Later Du Chong and Liu Kuo served as co-administrators of the Yanjing Branch Secretariat; laws were not yet unified and disputes arose daily, which Xiongxiang mediated.

sentences.zh: 曆深、磁州刺史，開封少尹，行台工部郎中，同知汴京留守事。

translations.literal: He served successively as prefect of Shen and Cizhou, junior administrator of Kaifeng, director in the Works Section of the Branch Secretariat, and co-administrator of the Bianjing regency.
translations.idiomatic: He served in turn as prefect of Shen and Cizhou, junior administrator of Kaifeng, director in the works section of the branch secretariat, and co-administrator of the Bianjing regency.

sentences.zh: 天德初，為山東東路轉運使，改鎮西軍節度使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tiande he was transport commissioner of the Eastern Shandong Circuit and was changed to military governor of the Zhenxi Army.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Tiande he became transport commissioner of the Eastern Shandong Circuit and was later made military governor of the Zhenxi Army.

sentences.zh: 是時，詔徐文、張弘信討東海縣，弘信逗遛，稱疾不進，決杖二百。

translations.literal: At that time an edict ordered Xu Wen and Zhang Hongxin to attack Donghai County; Hongxin delayed and claimed illness and would not advance, and was sentenced to two hundred blows with the staff.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Xu Wen and Zhang Hongxin were ordered to attack Donghai County; Hongxin lingered, pleaded illness, and refused to advance, and was sentenced to two hundred strokes of the staff.

sentences.zh: 熊祥被詔為會試主文，以「事不避難臣之職」為賦題。

translations.literal: Xiongxiang was ordered by edict to be chief examiner of the metropolitan examination, with the rhapsody topic "Not shunning hardship in affairs is the minister's duty."
translations.idiomatic: Xiongxiang was ordered to serve as chief examiner of the metropolitan examination, with the rhapsody topic "A minister's duty is not to shun hardship in affairs."

sentences.zh: 及禦試，熊祥複以「賞罰之令信如四時」為賦題，海陵大喜，以為翰林侍讀學士。

translations.literal: At the imperial examination Xiongxiang again set the rhapsody topic "Rewards and punishments' commands are trustworthy as the four seasons." Hailing was greatly pleased and made him Hanlin attendant reader.
translations.idiomatic: At the palace examination Xiongxiang again set the topic "Rewards and punishments are as trustworthy as the four seasons." Emperor Hailing was greatly pleased and appointed him Hanlin attendant reader.

sentences.zh: 大定初，起為太子少師。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Dading he was recalled and made Junior Tutor to the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Dading he was recalled and appointed junior tutor to the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 時契丹賊窩斡竊號，北鄙用兵未息，上以為憂，詔公卿百官議所以招伐之宜。

translations.literal: At that time the Khitan rebel Wohe usurped a title; on the northern frontier warfare had not ceased. The emperor was troubled by this and decreed that dukes, ministers, and the hundred officials deliberate on the proper means to summon and subdue him.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Khitan rebel Wohe had declared himself ruler and fighting on the northern frontier had not ceased. The emperor was troubled and ordered the chief ministers and officials to discuss how best to win him over or subdue him.

sentences.zh: 眾皆異議，熊祥徐進曰：「陛下以勞民為憂，用兵為重，莫若以恩信招懷之。」

translations.literal: All had differing opinions. Xiongxiang advanced slowly and said: "Your Majesty takes troubling the people as a worry and using troops as weighty—nothing is better than summoning and cherishing them with favor and trust."
translations.idiomatic: Everyone offered differing views. Xiongxiang stepped forward slowly and said: "Your Majesty is concerned for the people's labor and weighs the use of arms heavily—nothing is better than winning them with favor and trust."

sentences.zh: 上問：「孰可使者？」

translations.literal: The emperor asked: "Who can be sent?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked: "Who can be sent?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「臣雖老，憑國威靈，尚堪一行。」

translations.literal: He replied: "Though your subject is old, relying on the state's awesome spirit, I can still manage one journey."
translations.idiomatic: He replied: "Though I am old, relying on the state's authority I could still make the journey."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「卿老矣，無煩為此。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "You are old; do not trouble yourself with this."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "You are too old; do not trouble yourself with this."

sentences.zh: 七年，複致仕。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he again retired from office.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he retired from office again.

sentences.zh: 熊祥事母以孝聞，母沒時，熊祥年已七十，不食三日，人皆稱之。

translations.literal: Xiongxiang was known for filial service to his mother. When his mother died, Xiongxiang was already seventy; he did not eat for three days, and all praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Xiongxiang was renowned for filial devotion to his mother. When she died he was already seventy and fasted for three days, and all praised him.

sentences.zh: 卒於家。

translations.literal: He died at home.
translations.idiomatic: He died at home.

sentences.zh: 子 拯

translations.literal: Son: Zheng
translations.idiomatic: His son Zheng

sentences.zh: 拯字元濟。

translations.literal: Zheng, courtesy name Yuanji.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng, whose style name was Yuanji.

sentences.zh: 天德二年，定襲封衍聖公俸格，有加于常品。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tiande the salary scale for the hereditary enfeoffment as Duke Yansheng was fixed, with additions beyond the usual rank.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Tiande the salary scale for the hereditary Duke Yansheng was fixed, with emoluments above the usual rank.

sentences.zh: 是歲立國子監，久之，加拯承直郎。

translations.literal: That year the Directorate of Education was established; after long time Zheng was given the rank of Gentleman for Direct Service.
translations.idiomatic: That year the Directorate of Education was established; after some time Zheng was made gentleman for direct service.

sentences.zh: 大定元年卒。

translations.literal: He died in the first year of Dading.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the first year of Dading.

sentences.zh: 弟總襲封，加文林郎。

translations.literal: His younger brother Zong inherited the enfeoffment and was given the rank of Gentleman of Letters.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Zong inherited the title and was made gentleman of letters.

sentences.zh: 總字元會。

translations.literal: Zong, courtesy name Yuanhui.
translations.idiomatic: Zong, whose style name was Yuanhui.

sentences.zh: 大定二十年，召總至京師，欲與之官。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year of Dading Zong was summoned to the capital; the emperor wished to give him an office.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year of Dading Zong was summoned to the capital, and the emperor wished to appoint him to office.

sentences.zh: 尚書省奏：「總主先聖祀事，若加任使，守奉有闕。」

translations.literal: The Department of State Affairs memorialized: "Zong presides over the sacrifices to the Former Sage; if he is given further appointment, his maintenance of observance will be deficient."
translations.idiomatic: The Department of State Affairs reported: "Zong presides over the sacrifices to the Former Sage; if he is given another appointment, his ritual duties will suffer."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「然。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "It is so."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "That is so."

sentences.zh: 乃授曲阜縣令。

translations.literal: Thereupon he was appointed magistrate of Qufu County.
translations.idiomatic: He was therefore appointed magistrate of Qufu County.

sentences.zh: 明昌元年卒。

translations.literal: He died in the first year of Mingchang.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the first year of Mingchang.

sentences.zh: 子元措襲封，加文林郎。

translations.literal: His son Yuancuo inherited the enfeoffment and was given the rank of Gentleman of Letters.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yuancuo inherited the title and was made gentleman of letters.

sentences.zh: 元措字夢得。

translations.literal: Yuancuo, courtesy name Mengde.
translations.idiomatic: Yuancuo, whose style name was Mengde.

sentences.zh: 三年四月詔曰：「衍聖公視四品，階止八品，不稱。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the third year an edict said: "The Duke Yansheng is treated as fourth rank, yet his grade stops at eighth rank—this does not match.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the third year an edict said: "The Duke Yansheng is treated as fourth rank, yet his grade remains eighth—this is unfitting.

sentences.zh: 可超遷中議大夫，永著於令。」

translations.literal: He may be promoted beyond the norm to Grand Master of Palace Discourse and this be permanently written into the statutes."
translations.idiomatic: He may be promoted to grand master of palace discourse and this shall be permanently written into the statutes."

sentences.zh: 四年八月丁未，章宗行釋奠禮，北面再拜，親王、百官、六學生員陪位。

translations.literal: On dingwei day in the eighth month of the fourth year, Emperor Zhangzong performed the libation sacrifice to the sage, bowed twice facing north, and princes, the hundred officials, and students of the six schools attended in place.
translations.idiomatic: On dingwei day in the eighth month of the fourth year, Emperor Zhangzong performed the libation sacrifice to Confucius, bowed twice facing north, with princes, officials, and students of the six schools in attendance.

sentences.zh: 承安二年正月，詔元措兼曲阜縣令，仍世襲。

translations.literal: In the first month of the second year of Cheng'an, an edict made Yuancuo concurrently magistrate of Qufu County, still hereditary.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the second year of Cheng'an, an edict appointed Yuancuo concurrently magistrate of Qufu County, with the post still hereditary.

sentences.zh: 元措曆事宣宗、哀宗，後歸大元終焉。

translations.literal: Yuancuo served through Emperors Xuanzong and Aizong; afterward he submitted to the Great Yuan and ended his days there.
translations.idiomatic: Yuancuo served Emperors Xuanzong and Aizong; later he submitted to the Great Yuan and ended his life there.

sentences.zh: 四十八代端甫者，明昌初，學士党懷英薦其年德俱高，讀書樂道，該通古學。

translations.literal: Duanfu of the forty-eighth generation: at the beginning of Mingchang Academician Dang Huaiying recommended him, saying his years and virtue were both high, he read books and delighted in the Way, and was thoroughly versed in ancient learning.
translations.idiomatic: Duanfu of the forty-eighth generation: at the beginning of Mingchang Academician Dang Huaiying recommended him for his advanced years and virtue, his love of learning and the Way, and his mastery of classical studies.

sentences.zh: 召至京師，特賜王澤榜及第，除將仕郎、小學教授，以主簿半俸致仕。

translations.literal: He was summoned to the capital, specially granted passage on Wang Ze's examination list, appointed Gentleman for Initial Service and professor of the Primary School, and retired on half the salary of a registrar.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned to the capital, specially granted a pass on Wang Ze's examination list, appointed gentleman for initial service and professor of the primary school, and retired on half a registrar's salary.

sentences.zh: 范拱，字清叔，濟南人。

translations.literal: Fan Gong, courtesy name Qingshu, was a native of Jinan.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Gong, whose style name was Qingshu, came from Jinan.

sentences.zh: 九歲能屬文，深于《易》學。

translations.literal: At nine years of age he could compose literary pieces, and he was deeply versed in the study of the Book of Changes.
translations.idiomatic: By the age of nine he could already write essays, and he had an exceptional grasp of the Book of Changes.

sentences.zh: 宋末登進士第，調廣濟軍曹，權邦彥辟為書記，攝學事。

translations.literal: In the late Song he passed the jinshi examination, was assigned as an aide in the Guangji Army, was invited by Quan Bangyan to serve as a secretary, and acted in academic affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of the Song dynasty he earned his jinshi degree, took up a post in the Guangji Army, and was recruited by Quan Bangyan as a secretary, serving concurrently in academic administration.

sentences.zh: 劉豫鎮東平，拱撰謁廟文，豫奇之，深加賞識。

translations.literal: When Liu Yu governed Dongping, Gong composed a temple-visitation text; Yu found it remarkable and greatly prized and recognized him.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Yu was stationed at Dongping, Gong wrote an inscription for a temple visit. Liu Yu was impressed and held him in high regard.

sentences.zh: 拱獻《六箴》。

translations.literal: Gong presented the Six Admonitions.
translations.idiomatic: Gong submitted his Six Admonitions.

sentences.zh: 齊國建，累擢中書舍人。

translations.literal: When the Qi state was established, he was repeatedly promoted to Secretariat Drafter.
translations.idiomatic: After the Qi state was founded, he rose through successive promotions to the post of Secretariat Drafter.

sentences.zh: 上《初政錄》十五篇：一曰《得民》，二曰《命將》，三曰《簡禮》，四曰《納諫》，五曰《遠圖》，六曰《治亂》，七曰《舉賢》，八曰《守令》，九曰《延問》，十曰《畏慎》，十一曰《節祥瑞》十二曰《戒雷同》，十三曰《用人》，十四曰《禦將》，十五曰《禦軍》。

translations.literal: He submitted Records of Early Governance in fifteen chapters: I, "Winning the People"; II, "Appointing Generals"; III, "Simplifying Ritual"; IV, "Accepting Remonstrance"; V, "Long-range Planning"; VI, "Order and Disorder"; VII, "Advancing the Worthy"; VIII, "Prefects and Magistrates"; IX, "Extended Inquiry"; X, "Reverence and Caution"; XI, "Restraining Auspicious Omens"; XII, "Warning against Mechanical Conformity"; XIII, "Employing Men"; XIV, "Controlling Generals"; XV, "Controlling the Army".
translations.idiomatic: He presented Records of Early Governance in fifteen sections: "Winning the People," "Appointing Generals," "Simplifying Ritual," "Accepting Remonstrance," "Long-range Planning," "Order and Disorder," "Advancing the Worthy," "Prefects and Magistrates," "Extended Inquiry," "Reverence and Caution," "Restraining Auspicious Omens," "Warning against Mechanical Conformity," "Employing Men," "Controlling Generals," and "Controlling the Army."

sentences.zh: 豫納其說而不能盡用也。

translations.literal: Yu accepted his teachings but could not fully put them into practice.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu accepted his advice but was unable to implement it entirely.

sentences.zh: 久之，權尚書右丞，進左丞，兼門下侍郎。

translations.literal: After some time he served as Acting Vice Director of the Right in the Department of State Affairs, was promoted to Vice Director of the Left, and concurrently served as Vice Minister of the Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was appointed Acting Vice Director of the Right in the Department of State Affairs, then promoted to Vice Director of the Left while also serving as Vice Minister of the Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 豫以什一稅民，名為古法，其實裒斂，而刑法嚴急，吏夤緣為暴。

translations.literal: Yu taxed the people at one-tenth, calling it the ancient method, but in reality it was exaction; legal punishments were harsh and urgent, and officials used the occasion to act violently.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu levied a ten-percent tax on the people under the name of restoring an ancient practice, but in truth it was heavy extraction. Punishments were severe, and officials abused their power to commit abuse.

sentences.zh: 民久罹兵革，益窮困，陷罪者眾，境內苦之。

translations.literal: The people had long suffered warfare and became ever more destitute; many fell into crime, and the realm groaned under it.
translations.idiomatic: The people had endured war for years and were growing poorer. Convictions mounted, and suffering spread throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 右丞相張孝純及拱兄侍郎巽，極言其弊，請仍因履畝之法，豫不從。

translations.literal: Right Chancellor Zhang Xiaochun and Gong's elder brother, Vice Minister Xun, spoke strenuously of its abuses and asked to return to the method of assessing fields by acreage; Yu did not agree.
translations.idiomatic: Right Chancellor Zhang Xiaochun and Gong's elder brother Xun, a vice minister, pleaded vigorously against the policy and urged a return to field-acreage taxation, but Liu Yu refused.

sentences.zh: 巽坐貶官，自是無複敢言者。

translations.literal: Xun was punished by demotion, and from then on there was no one who dared speak again.
translations.idiomatic: Xun was demoted for his outspokenness, and after that no one dared raise the issue again.

sentences.zh: 拱曰：「吾言之則為党兄，不言則百姓困弊。

translations.literal: Gong said: "If I speak I will be accused of siding with my brother; if I do not speak the common people suffer distress.
translations.idiomatic: Gong said, "If I speak out, I will be charged with favoring my brother; if I stay silent, the people will continue to suffer.

sentences.zh: 吾執政也，甯為百姓言之。」

translations.literal: Since I hold office, I would rather speak for the common people."
translations.idiomatic: As one who holds office, I would rather speak on behalf of the people."

sentences.zh: 乃上疏，其大略以為「國家懲亡宋重斂弊，什一稅民，本務優恤，官吏奉行太急，驅民犯禁，非長久計也」。

translations.literal: He then submitted a memorial, the gist of which held that "the state, to learn from the disastrous heavy exactions of the fallen Song, taxed the people at one-tenth with the fundamental aim of generous relief, yet officials enforced it too urgently, driving the people to violate prohibitions—this is no long-term plan."
translations.idiomatic: He then submitted a memorial arguing that although the ten-percent tax had been meant to avoid the ruinous exactions of the fallen Song and to provide relief for the people, officials were enforcing it so harshly that they were driving people into crime—a policy that could not be sustained in the long run.

sentences.zh: 豫雖未即從，而亦不加譴。

translations.literal: Although Yu did not immediately follow it, he also did not reprimand him.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu did not adopt the proposal at once, but neither did he punish Gong for it.

sentences.zh: 拱令刑部條上諸路以稅抵罪者凡千餘人，豫見其多，乃更為五等稅法，民猶以為重也。

translations.literal: Gong had the Ministry of Punishments compile and report those in every circuit who had been convicted on account of tax—more than a thousand in all; when Yu saw how many there were, he revised the law into five grades of taxation, yet the people still found it heavy.
translations.idiomatic: Gong had the Ministry of Punishments catalog more than a thousand people throughout the circuits who had been convicted for tax offenses. When Liu Yu saw the number, he replaced the system with a five-tier tax law, but the people still regarded it as burdensome.

sentences.zh: 齊廢，梁王宗弼領行台省事，拱為官屬。

translations.literal: When Qi was abolished, Prince Zongbi of Liang took charge of the Regional Secretariat affairs, and Gong served among his staff.
translations.idiomatic: After the Qi state was dissolved, Prince Zongbi of Liang assumed control of the Regional Secretariat, and Gong served on his staff.

sentences.zh: 宗弼訪求百姓利病，拱以減稅為請，宗弼從之，減舊三分之一，民始蘇息。

translations.literal: Zongbi inquired into what harmed or benefited the common people; Gong asked that taxes be reduced, and Zongbi agreed, cutting the old rate by one-third, and the people at last recovered and rested.
translations.idiomatic: When Zongbi sought to learn what policies were harming or helping the people, Gong petitioned for tax reduction. Zongbi approved, cutting taxes by one-third, and the people finally began to recover.

sentences.zh: 拱慎許可，而推轂士，李南、張輔、劉長言皆拱薦也。

translations.literal: Gong was cautious in giving approval, yet he promoted scholars; Li Nan, Zhang Fu, and Liu Changyan were all recommended by Gong.
translations.idiomatic: Gong was sparing with his endorsements, but he actively promoted talent; Li Nan, Zhang Fu, and Liu Changyan were all men he recommended.

sentences.zh: 長言自汝州郟城酒監擢省郎，人不知其所以進，拱亦不自言也。

translations.literal: Changyan was promoted from wine supervisor of Jia County in Ruzhou to a provincial bureau officer; people did not know how he had advanced, and Gong also did not speak of it himself.
translations.idiomatic: Changyan rose from overseeing the wine monopoly in Jia County, Ruzhou, to a post in the central bureaucracy, and though no one knew how he had been promoted, Gong never said a word about it.

sentences.zh: 以久病乞近郡，除淄州刺史。

translations.literal: Because of long illness he requested a nearby prefecture and was appointed Prefect of Zi.
translations.idiomatic: Citing chronic illness, he asked for a nearby post and was appointed prefect of Zi Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 皇統四年，以疾求退，以通議大夫致仕。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Huangtong, because of illness he sought retirement and retired with the rank of Grand Master for Extended Discussion.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of the Huangtong era, he requested retirement on grounds of illness and left office with the rank of Grand Master for Extended Discussion.

sentences.zh: 齋居讀書，罕對妻子。

translations.literal: He lived in abstemious retirement reading books, rarely meeting with wife and children.
translations.idiomatic: He lived simply at home with his books and seldom saw even his wife and children.

sentences.zh: 世宗在濟南聞其名。

translations.literal: Shizong, while in Jinan, heard his name.
translations.idiomatic: While in Jinan, Emperor Shizong heard of his reputation.

sentences.zh: 大定初，拱上封事。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Dading era, Gong submitted a sealed memorial.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Dading era, Gong submitted a memorial to the throne.

sentences.zh: 七年，召赴闕，除太常卿。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was summoned to court and appointed Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he was summoned to court and made Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 議郊祀。

translations.literal: He deliberated on the suburban sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: He took part in deliberations on the suburban sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 或有言前代都長安及汴、洛，乙太、華等山列為五嶽，今既都燕，當別議五嶽名。

translations.literal: Some said that earlier dynasties with capitals at Chang'an, Bian, and Luoyang had ordered Mount Tai, Mount Hua, and others to be listed among the Five Sacred Mountains; now that the capital was at Yan, the names of the Five Mountains should be reconsidered separately.
translations.idiomatic: Some argued that when past dynasties had capitals at Chang'an, Bian, and Luoyang, they had designated Mount Tai, Mount Hua, and others as the Five Sacred Mountains, and that now, with the capital at Yan, a new set of five mountains ought to be chosen.

sentences.zh: 寺僚取《崧高》疏「周都酆鎬，以吳嶽為西嶽」。

translations.literal: The officials of the court cited the commentary on Song Gao: "Zhou's capital was at Feng and Hao, and Mount Wu was taken as the Western Peak."
translations.idiomatic: Officials in the court cited a commentary on Song Gao stating that when Zhou had its capital at Feng and Hao, Mount Wu had served as the Western Peak.

sentences.zh: 拱以為非是，議略曰：「軒轅居上穀，在恆山之西，舜居蒲阪，在華山之北。

translations.literal: Gong held this incorrect, and his discussion in brief said: "Huangdi dwelt at Shanggu, west of Mount Heng; Shun dwelt at Puban, north of Mount Hua.
translations.idiomatic: Gong disagreed, arguing in outline: "The Yellow Emperor lived at Shanggu, west of Mount Heng, and Shun lived at Puban, north of Mount Hua.

sentences.zh: 以此言之，未嘗據所都而改嶽祀也。」

translations.literal: Judging by this, they never altered the worship of the peaks according to where they had their capital."
translations.idiomatic: From this it is clear that they never changed which mountains were worshipped simply because they moved their capital."

sentences.zh: 後遂不改。

translations.literal: Thereafter it was not changed after all.
translations.idiomatic: In the end the designations were not changed.

sentences.zh: 拱嘗言：「禮官當守禮，法官當守法，若漢張釋之可謂能守法矣。」

translations.literal: Gong once said: "Officers of ritual should uphold ritual; officers of law should uphold law—Han Zhang Shizhi may be said to have been able to uphold the law."
translations.idiomatic: Gong once remarked, "Ritual officials should uphold ritual, and legal officials should uphold the law. In the Han dynasty, Zhang Shizhi showed what it meant truly to uphold the law."

sentences.zh: 故其議論確然不可移奪。

translations.literal: Therefore his discussions were firm and could not be shifted or overturned.
translations.idiomatic: His opinions were therefore firm and not easily swayed.

sentences.zh: 九年，複致仕，卒於家，年七十四。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he retired again, died at home, aged seventy-four.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he retired once more, then died at home at the age of seventy-four.

sentences.zh: 張用直

translations.literal: Zhang Yongzhi
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yongzhi

sentences.zh: 劉樞，字居中，通州三河人。

translations.literal: Liu Shu, courtesy name Juzhong, was a native of Sanhe in Tongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Shu, styled Juzhong, was from Sanhe in Tongzhou.

sentences.zh: 少以良家子從軍，屯河間。

translations.literal: In youth, as the son of a good household, he joined the army and was garrisoned at Hejian.
translations.idiomatic: As a young man from a respectable family, he entered military service and was stationed at Hejian.

sentences.zh: 同輩皆騎射，獨樞刻意經史。

translations.literal: His comrades all practiced horsemanship and archery; only Shu devoted himself earnestly to the classics and histories.
translations.idiomatic: While his comrades devoted themselves to horsemanship and archery, Shu alone applied himself to the classics and histories.

sentences.zh: 登天眷二年進士，調唐山主簿。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination in the second year of Tianjuan and was assigned as recorder of Tangshan.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the second year of the Tianjuan era and was appointed recorder of Tangshan County.

sentences.zh: 改飛狐令，蔚州刺史恃功貪污無所顧忌，屬邑皆厭苦之，樞一無所應，乃摭以他事系獄，將致之死。

translations.literal: He was transferred to be magistrate of Feihu; the Prefect of Yu relied on his merits, was greedy and corrupt without restraint, and all subordinate counties loathed and suffered under him; Shu would not comply at all, so the prefect seized on other matters to imprison him, intending to bring him to death.
translations.idiomatic: He was reassigned as magistrate of Feihu. The prefect of Yu Prefecture, emboldened by his past service, was corrupt and feared no restraint, and every subordinate county resented him. When Shu refused to cooperate, the prefect fabricated charges, threw him in prison, and sought to have him executed.

sentences.zh: 郡人有憐樞者，導樞脫走，訴於朝。

translations.literal: A man in the prefecture who pitied Shu guided him to escape, and he appealed to the court.
translations.idiomatic: A sympathetic local man helped Shu escape, and Shu appealed to the central court.

sentences.zh: 會廉察使至，守倅而下皆抵罪廢，獨樞治狀入優等，躐遷奉直大夫。

translations.literal: When the integrity commissioner arrived, the prefect, vice-prefect, and all below were convicted and dismissed; Shu alone had his record of governance rated in the superior grade and was abruptly promoted to Grand Master for Direct Counsel.
translations.idiomatic: When an integrity commissioner arrived, the prefect, his deputy, and their subordinates were all convicted and removed from office. Shu alone received the highest rating for his governance and was promoted directly to Grand Master for Direct Counsel.

sentences.zh: 張浩營建燕京宮室，選樞分治工役。

translations.literal: Zhang Hao was constructing the palaces at Yanjing; Shu was selected to share in managing the labor duties.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Hao oversaw construction of the palaces at Yanjing, Shu was chosen to help manage the labor assignments.

sentences.zh: 遷尚書刑部員外郎，鞫治太原尹徒單阿裏出虎反狀，旬日獄具。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Vice Director in the Ministry of Punishments of the Department of State Affairs and investigated the treason case of Taiyuan Governor Tushan Ali Chuhu; within ten days the case was complete.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Vice Director in the Ministry of Punishments and investigated the treason case of Taiyuan Governor Tushan Ali Chuhu, completing the trial within ten days.

sentences.zh: 轉工部郎中，進本部侍郎。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Director in the Ministry of Works and advanced to Vice Minister of that ministry.
translations.idiomatic: He moved to Director in the Ministry of Works and then rose to Vice Minister of the same ministry.

sentences.zh: 正隆末，從軍還自江上。

translations.literal: At the end of the Zhenglong era he returned from military service on the Yangzi.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of the Zhenglong era he returned from military service along the Yangzi.

sentences.zh: 大定初，與左司郎中王蔚、右司員外郎王全俱出補外，樞為南京路轉運使事。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Dading, together with Left Department Director Wang Wei and Right Department Vice Director Wang Quan he all went out to fill external posts; Shu served as Commissioner of Transport for the Nanjing Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Dading era, he was sent out with Left Department Director Wang Wei and Right Department Vice Director Wang Quan to provincial posts; Shu became Commissioner of Transport for the Nanjing Circuit.

sentences.zh: 初，世宗欲複用樞等，御史台奏：「樞等在正隆時皆以巧進，敗法蠹政，人多怨嫉之。」

translations.literal: At first Shizong wished to employ Shu and the others again; the Censorate memorialized: "Shu and the others in the Zhenglong era all advanced by artifice, ruined the law and harmed government, and many resented and envied them."
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shizong wished to reappoint Shu and the others, the Censorate reported, "During the Zhenglong era, Shu and his colleagues had risen through flattery, undermining the law and corrupting government, and they were widely resented."

sentences.zh: 上以樞等頗幹濟，猶用之，戒之曰：「能悛心改過，必加升擢。

translations.literal: The emperor, because Shu and the others were fairly capable in administration, still employed them and admonished them: "If you can repent in heart and reform your faults, you will surely be further promoted.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, judging them still capable administrators, reappointed them anyway, warning, "If you truly repent and reform, you will be promoted;

sentences.zh: 不然，則斥汝等矣。」

translations.literal: Otherwise, I will dismiss you all."
translations.idiomatic: otherwise I will dismiss every one of you."

sentences.zh: 是時，阿勒根彥忠為南京都轉運使，不閑吏事，故用樞以佐之。

translations.literal: At that time Aligen Yanzhong was Chief Commissioner of Transport for Nanjing and was unskilled in administrative affairs, so Shu was used to assist him.
translations.idiomatic: At the time, Aligen Yanzhong served as Chief Commissioner of Transport for Nanjing but lacked experience in administration, so Shu was appointed to assist him.

sentences.zh: 遷山東路轉運使，改中都路轉運使。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Commissioner of Transport for the Shandong Circuit and then changed to Commissioner of Transport for the Central Capital Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Commissioner of Transport for the Shandong Circuit, then reassigned as Commissioner of Transport for the Central Capital Circuit.

sentences.zh: 大定四年，卒於官。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Dading he died in office.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of the Dading era, he died while still in office.

sentences.zh: 王翛，字翛然，涿州人也。

translations.literal: Wang Xiao, courtesy name Xiaoran, was a man of Zhuo Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xiao, styled Xiaoran, was from Zhuo Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 登皇統二年進士第，由尚書省令史除同知霸州事。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination in the second year of Huangtong and from a clerk in the Department of State Affairs was appointed Vice Administrator of Ba Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: After passing the jinshi examination in the second year of the Huangtong era, he rose from a clerk in the Department of State Affairs to Vice Administrator of Ba Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 累遷刑部員外郎。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Vice Director in the Ministry of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted through successive posts to Vice Director in the Ministry of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 坐請囑故人奸罪，杖四十，降授泰定軍節度副使。

translations.literal: Because he had interceded for an old acquaintance in a treason case, he was flogged forty strokes and demoted to Vice Military Commissioner of the Taide Army.
translations.idiomatic: He was convicted of using personal influence to reduce charges against an old acquaintance in a treason case, flogged forty strokes, and demoted to Vice Military Commissioner of the Taide Army.

sentences.zh: 四遷大興府治中，授戶部侍郎。

translations.literal: After four promotions he became Administrator of Daxing Prefecture and was appointed Vice Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: After four further promotions he became Administrator of Daxing Prefecture and was appointed Vice Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 世宗謂宰臣曰：「王翛前為外官，聞有剛直名。

translations.literal: Shizong said to the chief ministers: "Wang Xiao, when he previously served as an outside official, was heard to have a reputation for stern uprightness.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shizong told his chief ministers, "When Wang Xiao served in the provinces, he had a reputation for uncompromising integrity.

sentences.zh: 今聞專務出罪為陰德，事多非理從輕。

translations.literal: Now I hear he specializes in acquitting offenders as hidden virtue, and in many cases unreasonably lightens sentences.
translations.idiomatic: Now I hear he specializes in acquitting the guilty as a form of secret merit, lightly dismissing cases that ought to be punished.

sentences.zh: 又巧幸偷安，若果剛直，則當忘身以為國，履正以無偏，何必賣法以徼福耶？」

translations.literal: Again he is clever at seeking safety—if he were truly stern and upright, he ought to forget himself for the state, walk the straight path without partiality—why must he sell the law to beg for blessing?"
translations.idiomatic: He is also adept at looking out for himself. If he were truly upright, he would risk himself for the state and apply the law without favor—why would he distort the law to curry favor?"

sentences.zh: 尋命賑濟密雲等三十六縣猛安人戶，冒請粟三萬余石，為尚書省奏奪官一階，出為同知北京留守事。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was ordered to provide relief to the meng'an households of thirty-six counties including Miyun; he falsely claimed more than thirty thousand shi of grain, and the Department of State Affairs memorialized to strip him of one rank; he was sent out as Vice Administrator of the Northern Capital Military Commission.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after, he was tasked with distributing relief to military colonist households in thirty-six counties including Miyun. He fraudulently claimed more than thirty thousand shi of grain and was stripped of one rank by memorial from the Department of State Affairs, then demoted to Vice Administrator of the Northern Capital Military Commission.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「人多言王翛能官，以朕觀之，凡事不肯盡力，直一老奸耳。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Many say Wang Xiao is a capable official, but in my view he refuses to exert himself in all matters—he is simply an old schemer."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Many praise Wang Xiao as an able official, but from my perspective he never applies himself fully to anything. He is nothing but a crafty old opportunist."

sentences.zh: 二十四年，遷遼東路轉運使。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year he was transferred to Commissioner of Transport for the Liaodong Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fourth year he was transferred to Commissioner of Transport for the Liaodong Circuit.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，改顯德軍節度使。

translations.literal: After a little more than a year he was changed to Military Commissioner of the Xiande Army.
translations.idiomatic: A little over a year later he was reassigned as Military Commissioner of the Xiande Army.

sentences.zh: 以前任轉運使拽辱倉使王祺致死，追兩官解職，敕杖七十，降授鄭州防禦使。

translations.literal: Because as former Commissioner of Transport he humiliated and dragged Warehouse Commissioner Wang Qi to death, two ranks were stripped and he was removed from office, ordered flogged seventy strokes, and demoted to Defense Commissioner of Zheng Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Because as a former transport commissioner he had humiliated Warehouse Commissioner Wang Qi to the point of death, he was stripped of two ranks, dismissed from office, ordered flogged seventy strokes, and demoted to Defense Commissioner of Zheng Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 章宗即位，擢同知大興府事。

translations.literal: When Zhangzong ascended the throne, he was promoted to Vice Administrator of Daxing Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhangzong took the throne, he was promoted to Vice Administrator of Daxing Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 審錄官奏，翛前任顯德潔廉剛直，軍吏斂跡，無訟獄。

translations.literal: The review officer memorialized that in Xiao's previous post at Xiande he was clean, incorrupt, and sternly upright; military officials restrained themselves and there were no lawsuits or prisons.
translations.idiomatic: A review officer reported that during Xiao's earlier tenure at Xiande he had been incorruptible and resolute, so that military officials held themselves in check and lawsuits disappeared.

sentences.zh: 遷禮部尚書，兼大理卿。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Minister of Rites and concurrently served as Director of the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Minister of Rites while also serving as Director of the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 使宋還，會改葬太師廣平郡王徒單貞。

translations.literal: Returning from an embassy to Song, he arrived when Grand Preceptor and Prince of Guangping, Tushan Zhen, was being reburied.
translations.idiomatic: After returning from an embassy to the Song, he arrived just as Grand Preceptor Tushan Zhen, Prince of Guangping, was being reinterred.

sentences.zh: 貞，章宗母孝懿皇后父也。

translations.literal: Zhen was the father of Empress Xiaoyi, Zhangzong's mother.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen was the father of Empress Xiaoyi, the mother of Emperor Zhangzong.

sentences.zh: 帝欲用前代故事，班劍、鼓吹、羽葆等儀衛。

translations.literal: The emperor wished to follow the precedents of earlier dynasties—ceremonial guards with gilded swords, musical escort, feathered parasols, and other such ritual attendants.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wished to follow precedents from earlier dynasties by granting ceremonial guards, a musical escort, feathered parasols, and other such honors for the funeral.

sentences.zh: 宰臣以貞與弑熙宗誅死，意難之。

translations.literal: The chief ministers, because Zhen had been executed for regicide against Xizong, found it difficult in principle.
translations.idiomatic: The chief ministers objected on the grounds that Zhen had been executed for involvement in Emperor Xizong's assassination.

sentences.zh: 於是詔下禮官議。

translations.literal: Thereupon an edict was issued ordering the ritual officials to deliberate.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then ordered the ritual officials to deliberate on the matter.

sentences.zh: 翛言：「晉葬丞相王導，給前後羽葆、鼓吹、武賁、班劍百人。

translations.literal: Xiao said: "When Jin buried Chancellor Wang Dao, he was granted before and behind feathered parasols, musical escort, military guards, and a hundred men with gilded swords.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao argued, "When the Jin dynasty buried Chancellor Wang Dao, the funeral included feathered parasols, a musical escort, military guards, and a hundred sword-bearers in ceremonial dress.

sentences.zh: 唐以來，大駕鹵簿有班劍，其王公以下鹵簿並無班劍，兼羽葆非臣下所宜用，國朝葬大臣亦無之。」

translations.literal: From Tang onward, the great imperial procession guard had gilded swords, but the procession guards of kings, dukes, and those below had none; moreover feathered parasols are not what subjects should properly use—in our dynasty too, when burying great ministers there has been none of this."
translations.idiomatic: From the Tang dynasty onward, gilded swords appeared only in the emperor's procession. Lesser ranks were not granted them, and feathered parasols were never appropriate for subjects. Our dynasty too has never granted such honors at the funerals of ministers."

sentences.zh: 上先知唐葬大臣李靖等皆用班劍、羽葆，怒曰：「典故所無，固可從，然用之亦不過禮。」

translations.literal: The emperor, knowing beforehand that when Tang buried great ministers such as Li Jing they all used gilded swords and feathered parasols, said angrily: "What the precedent records do not contain may surely be followed, yet to use them would not exceed ritual propriety."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, already aware that Tang ministers such as Li Jing had been granted gilded swords and feathered parasols at their funerals, said angrily, "What your precedents omit may be set aside, but granting these honors would not exceed proper ritual."

sentences.zh: 一日，詔翛及諫議大夫兼禮部侍郎張暐詣殿門，諭之曰：「朝廷之事，汝諫官、禮官即當辯析。

translations.literal: One day he ordered Xiao and Remonstrating Grand Master and concurrent Vice Minister of Rites Zhang Wei to come to the palace gate and instructed them: "On affairs of court, you remonstrating officials and ritual officials should at once analyze and explain.
translations.idiomatic: One day he summoned Xiao and Remonstrating Grand Master Zhang Wei, who also served as Vice Minister of Rites, to the palace gate and told them, "On matters of state, you as remonstrating and ritual officials should speak your minds clearly.

sentences.zh: 且小民言可采，朕尚從之，況卿等乎？

translations.literal: Moreover, when common people's words may be adopted, I still follow them—how much more you, gentlemen?
translations.idiomatic: When even commoners offer useful advice, I listen. How much more should I hear from officials such as you?

sentences.zh: 自今議事，毋但附合尚書省。」

translations.literal: From today when deliberating matters, do not merely echo the Department of State Affairs."
translations.idiomatic: From now on, when you deliberate, do not simply echo whatever the Department of State Affairs proposes."

sentences.zh: 明昌二年，改知大興府事。

translations.literal: In the second year of Mingchang he was changed to Administrator of Daxing Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of the Mingchang era he was reassigned as Administrator of Daxing Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 時僧徒多游貴戚門，翛惡之，乃禁僧午後不得出寺。

translations.literal: At the time many Buddhist monks frequented the houses of noble kindred; Xiao disliked this and prohibited monks from leaving their temples after noon.
translations.idiomatic: At the time many monks spent their afternoons visiting the mansions of great families. Xiao despised the practice and forbade monks to leave their temples after noon.

sentences.zh: 嘗一僧犯禁，皇姑大長公主為請，翛曰：「奉主命，即令出之。」

translations.literal: Once a monk violated the prohibition; the Grand Eldest Princess, the emperor's aunt, interceded for him; Xiao said: "Obeying the princess's command, I will at once order his release."
translations.idiomatic: When one monk broke the rule, the Grand Eldest Princess, the emperor's aunt, interceded on his behalf. Xiao replied, "If I must obey Her Highness, I will release him at once."

sentences.zh: 立召僧，杖一百死，京師肅然。

translations.literal: He immediately summoned the monk, flogged him a hundred strokes to death, and the capital became somber and orderly.
translations.idiomatic: He then had the monk brought out, flogged a hundred strokes until he died, and the capital fell silent.

sentences.zh: 後坐故出人罪，複削官解職。

translations.literal: Later, because he improperly acquitted offenders, his rank was again stripped and he was removed from office.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was again stripped of rank and dismissed for improperly acquitting offenders.

sentences.zh: 明年，特授定海軍節度使。

translations.literal: The next year he was specially appointed Military Commissioner of the Dinghai Army.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was specially reappointed Military Commissioner of the Dinghai Army.

sentences.zh: 諭旨曰：「卿賦性太剛，率意行事，乃自陷於刑。

translations.literal: The instructive edict said: "Your nature is too stubborn; acting according to your own impulse, you entangled yourself in punishment.
translations.idiomatic: The edict read, "Your nature is too unyielding; acting on impulse, you brought punishment upon yourself.

sentences.zh: 若殿年降敘，念卿入仕久，頗有執持，故特起於罪謫之中，授以見職。

translations.literal: If one merely considered years in rank and reduced appointment, yet mindful that you have long entered office and have considerable firmness of purpose, I therefore specially raise you from among guilt and exile and grant a visible post.
translations.idiomatic: By seniority alone you would remain demoted, but considering your long service and your firmness of character, I am restoring you from disgrace to an active post.

sentences.zh: 且彼歲歉民饑，盜賊多，須用舊人鎮撫，庶得安治。

translations.literal: Moreover that region has lean harvests and hungry people, with many bandits; an old hand is needed to pacify and soothe, so that peace and order may be attained.
translations.idiomatic: That region has suffered failed harvests, famine, and widespread banditry. It needs an experienced man to restore order.

sentences.zh: 勉晝乃心，以圖後效。」

translations.literal: Strive with all your heart by day to seek later results."
translations.idiomatic: Apply yourself wholeheartedly and prove your worth anew."

sentences.zh: 未幾，表乞致仕。

translations.literal: Before long he submitted a memorial requesting retirement.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he submitted a memorial requesting retirement.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「翛能幹者，得力為多。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Among the capable, Xiao is one from whom much force may be drawn."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Among capable officials, Xiao is one of the most useful."

sentences.zh: 不許。

translations.literal: He did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: The request was denied.

sentences.zh: 複申請，從之。

translations.literal: He petitioned again, and the request was granted.
translations.idiomatic: When he petitioned again, the emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 泰和七年，卒，年七十五。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Taihe he died, aged seventy-five.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of the Taihe era he died at the age of seventy-five.

sentences.zh: 翛性剛嚴，臨事果決，吏民憚其威，雖豪右不敢犯。

translations.literal: Xiao's nature was stern and severe; in affairs he was resolute and decisive; officials and people feared his authority, and even powerful families did not dare offend.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao was stern and forceful, decisive in action, and feared by officials and commoners alike—even the powerful did not dare cross him.

sentences.zh: 承安間，知大興府事闕，詔諭宰臣曰：「可選極有風力如王翛輩者用之。」

translations.literal: During the Cheng'an era, when the post of Administrator of Daxing Prefecture was vacant, an edict instructed the chief ministers: "You may select one of extremely strong force of character like Wang Xiao for appointment."
translations.idiomatic: During the Cheng'an era, when the post of Administrator of Daxing Prefecture fell vacant, the emperor instructed his ministers, "Choose someone with exceptional force of character, a man in the mold of Wang Xiao."

sentences.zh: 其為上所知如此。

translations.literal: Such was the esteem in which the sovereign held him.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the esteem in which the throne held him.

sentences.zh: 楊伯雄

translations.literal: Yang Boxiong
translations.idiomatic: Yang Boxiong

sentences.zh: 楊伯雄，字希雲，真定槁城人。

translations.literal: Yang Boxiong, courtesy name Xiyun, was a native of Gaocheng in Zhending.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Boxiong, whose style name was Xiyun, came from Gaocheng in Zhending Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 八世祖彥稠，後唐清泰中為定州兵馬使。

translations.literal: His eighth-generation ancestor Yanchou, in the Qingtai era of Later Tang, served as military commissioner of Dingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Eight generations back, his ancestor Yanchou had served as military commissioner of Dingzhou during the Qingtai reign of Later Tang.

sentences.zh: 後隨晉主北遷，遂居臨潢。

translations.literal: Later he followed the Jin ruler northward in migration and settled at Linhuang.
translations.idiomatic: He later followed the Jin court in its northward move and made his home at Linhuang.

sentences.zh: 父丘行，太子左衛率府率。

translations.literal: His father was Qiu Xing, captain of the Left Guard Office of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: His father, Qiu Xing, held the post of captain in the Left Guard Office of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 伯雄登皇統二年進士，海陵留守中京，丘行在幕府，伯雄來省視，海陵見之，深加器重。

translations.literal: Boxiong passed the jinshi examination in the second year of Huangtong. Hailing was stationed at Zhongjing as regent; Qiu Xing was in his staff, and Boxiong came to visit him. Hailing saw him and greatly valued him.
translations.idiomatic: Boxiong placed on the jinshi rolls in the second year of Huangtong. While Hailing was holding Zhongjing as regent, Qiu Xing served on his staff; when Boxiong came to visit his father, Hailing met him and came to hold him in high regard.

sentences.zh: 久之，調韓州軍事判官。

translations.literal: After some time he was transferred as military affairs adjudicator of Hanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was appointed military affairs adjudicator at Hanzhou.

sentences.zh: 有二盜詐稱賈販，逆旅主人見欺，至州署陳訴，實欲劫取伯雄。

translations.literal: Two bandits falsely claimed to be merchants. The innkeeper, having been deceived, came to the prefectural office to lodge a complaint; their real intent was to rob Boxiong.
translations.idiomatic: Two robbers had posed as traveling merchants. Their victim, the innkeeper, came to the prefectural yamen to lodge a complaint—a complaint that was in fact a ruse to waylay Boxiong.

sentences.zh: 伯雄心覺其詐，執而詰之，並獲其党十餘人，一郡駭服。

translations.literal: Boxiong sensed in his heart that it was a ruse; he seized and interrogated them, and also captured more than ten of their accomplices. The whole prefecture was awed into submission.
translations.idiomatic: Boxiong sensed the fraud at once. He seized the men and questioned them, then rounded up more than a dozen of their accomplices as well, leaving the whole district stunned into respect.

sentences.zh: 遷應奉翰林文字。

translations.literal: He was promoted to drafter in the Hanlin Academy of Responding to Imperial Command.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Hanlin drafter in the Responding to Imperial Command Academy.

sentences.zh: 是時，海陵執政，自以舊知伯雄，屬之使時時至其第，伯雄諾之而不往也。

translations.literal: At that time Hailing held power. Considering himself an old acquaintance of Boxiong, he asked him to come frequently to his residence. Boxiong agreed but did not go.
translations.idiomatic: Hailing was then in charge of the government and, claiming an old tie with Boxiong, asked him to visit his house often. Boxiong assented—and never went.

sentences.zh: 他日海陵怪問之，對曰：「君子受知于人當以禮進，附麗奔走，非素志也。」

translations.literal: Another day Hailing, wondering, asked him about it. He replied: "When a gentleman receives another's recognition, he should advance by ritual propriety. Clinging and running about in attendance was never my original resolve.
translations.idiomatic: On another occasion Hailing asked him why. Boxiong answered, "When a gentleman has won another's esteem, he should approach him through proper ceremony. To hang on his patron's sleeve and scurry about at his command—that was never what I meant to become."

sentences.zh: 由是愈厚待之。

translations.literal: From this he treated him all the more generously.
translations.idiomatic: After that Hailing treated him with even greater favor.

sentences.zh: 海陵篡立，數月，遷右補闕，改修起居注。

translations.literal: After Hailing usurped the throne, within several months Boxiong was promoted to Right Supplements Censor and transferred to Compiler of the Diary of Activity and Repose.
translations.idiomatic: Within months of Hailing's usurpation, Boxiong was made Right Supplements Censor and then transferred to compiler of the imperial diary.

sentences.zh: 海陵銳於求治，講論每至夜分。

translations.literal: Hailing was keen to seek good governance; discussions often lasted until midnight.
translations.idiomatic: Hailing was eager to govern well, and their discussions often ran deep into the night.

sentences.zh: 嘗問曰：「人君治天下，其道何貴？」

translations.literal: Once he asked: "When a ruler governs all under Heaven, what is most prized in the Way?
translations.idiomatic: He once asked, "When a ruler sets the realm in order, what principle should he value above all?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「貴靜。」

translations.literal: He replied: "Stillness is prized.
translations.idiomatic: Boxiong answered, "Stillness."

sentences.zh: 海陵默然。

translations.literal: Hailing fell silent.
translations.idiomatic: Hailing said nothing.

sentences.zh: 明日，複謂曰：「我遷諸部猛安分屯邊戍，前夕之對，豈指是為非靜邪？」

translations.literal: The next day he said again: "I am transferring the meng'an of the various tribes to garrison the borders in dispersed posts. Did your reply last night mean that this is not stillness?
translations.idiomatic: The next day he said, "I have been relocating the tribal meng'an to scattered border garrisons. Last night, when you praised stillness—were you saying that policy is wrong?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「徙兵分屯，使南北相維，長策也。

translations.literal: He replied: "Moving troops to garrison in dispersed posts, so that north and south support each other, is a long-term strategy.
translations.idiomatic: Boxiong replied, "Dispersing troops along the frontier so that north and south hold each other up—that is sound long-term policy.

sentences.zh: 所謂靜者，乃不擾之耳。」

translations.literal: What is called stillness is simply not troubling the people.
translations.idiomatic: By stillness I meant only that the people should not be disturbed."

sentences.zh: 乙夜，複問鬼神事。

translations.literal: At the second watch of the night, he again asked about ghosts and spirits.
translations.idiomatic: Deep into the night he raised the subject of ghosts and spirits again.

sentences.zh: 伯雄進曰：「漢文帝召見賈生，夜半前席，不問百姓而問鬼神，後世頗譏之。

translations.literal: Boxiong stepped forward and said: "When Emperor Wen of Han summoned Jia Yi, at midnight he moved forward his mat, yet asked not about the common people but about ghosts and spirits. Later ages have largely ridiculed this.
translations.idiomatic: Boxiong stepped forward. "When Emperor Wen of Han received Jia Yi at midnight and drew his mat close, he asked about ghosts and spirits rather than the people—a choice later ages have not ceased to mock.

sentences.zh: 陛下不以臣愚陋，幸及天下大計，鬼神之事，未之學也。」

translations.literal: Your Majesty does not regard your servant as stupid and crude and has graciously let me reach the great plans for all under Heaven, but affairs of ghosts and spirits I have not studied.
