translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty has been kind enough not to despise me as dull and unlearned, and to consult me on the great affairs of the realm. Ghosts and spirits, however, I have never studied."

sentences.zh: 海陵曰：「但言之，以釋永夜倦思。」

translations.literal: Hailing said: "Just speak of it, to relieve the weariness of thought on this endless night.
translations.idiomatic: Hailing said, "Say what you will—it will break the tedium of a long night."

sentences.zh: 伯雄不得已，乃曰：「臣家有一卷書，記人死複生，或問冥官何以免罪，答曰，汝置一曆，白日所為，暮夜書之，不可書者是不可為也。」

translations.literal: Boxiong, having no choice, then said: "In my family there is a scroll that records a man's death and return to life. Someone asked the underworld official how guilt might be avoided. The answer was: Make a calendar; record by night what you did by day. What cannot be written cannot be done.
translations.idiomatic: Unable to refuse, Boxiong said, "At home we have an old book that tells of a man who died and came back to life. When someone asked the judge of the dead how to avoid guilt, the answer was: Keep a ledger—write down each day's deeds each night. What you cannot write down, you must not do."

sentences.zh: 海陵為之改容。

translations.literal: At this Hailing changed his expression.
translations.idiomatic: Hailing's face changed at the words.

sentences.zh: 夏日，海陵登瑞雲樓納涼，命伯雄賦詩，其卒章雲：「六月不知蒸鬱到，清涼會與萬方同。」

translations.literal: In summer Hailing ascended Ruiyun Tower to enjoy the cool air and ordered Boxiong to compose a poem. Its closing lines read: "In the sixth month one does not know the steaming heat has come; cool refreshment will be shared with the myriad regions.
translations.idiomatic: One summer day Hailing climbed Ruiyun Tower to escape the heat and asked Boxiong for a poem. Its closing lines ran: "Even in the sixth month, let no one feel the weight of the heat—may coolness be shared with all under Heaven.

sentences.zh: 海陵忻然，以示左右曰：「伯雄出語不忘規戒，為人臣當如是矣。」

translations.literal: Hailing was pleased and, showing it to those at his side, said: "Boxiong's words never forget admonition and warning. A minister should be like this.
translations.idiomatic: Hailing was delighted and showed the poem to his attendants. "Even in verse Boxiong never forgets to admonish," he said. "That is how a minister ought to be."

sentences.zh: 再遷兵部員外郎。

translations.literal: He was again promoted to Vice Director in the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: Boxiong was soon promoted again, to vice director in the Ministry of War.

sentences.zh: 丁父憂，起複翰林待制，兼修起居注。

translations.literal: When his father died he entered mourning, then was recalled from mourning as Hanlin Awaiting Orders and concurrently continued as Compiler of the Diary of Activity and Repose.
translations.idiomatic: After his father's death he observed mourning, then was recalled to serve as Hanlin awaiting orders while continuing as compiler of the imperial diary.

sentences.zh: 遷直學士，再遷右諫議大夫，兼著作郎，修起居注如故。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Direct Academician, then again to Right Remonstrating Grand Master, concurrently Author and Compiler, and continued the Diary of Activity and Repose as before.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to direct academician, then to right remonstrating grand master, also serving as author and compiler while retaining his post on the imperial diary.

sentences.zh: 六年，上幸西京，欲因往涼陘避暑，伯雄率眾諫官入諫。

translations.literal: In the sixth year the emperor visited the Western Capital and wished to proceed from there to Liangjing to escape the summer heat. Boxiong led the remonstrating officials in memorializing against it.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year the emperor went to the Western Capital and planned to continue on to Liangjing for the summer. Boxiong led his fellow remonstrators in urging him not to go.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「朕徐思之。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "I shall think on it at length.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "I will think it over."

sentences.zh: 伯雄言之不已，同列皆引退，久之乃起。

translations.literal: Boxiong spoke without stopping. His colleagues all withdrew; only after a long time did he rise.
translations.idiomatic: Boxiong would not leave off. His colleagues slipped away one by one; he alone remained, and only after a long while did he rise to go.

sentences.zh: 是年，至涼陘，徼巡果有疏虞。

translations.literal: That year, when he reached Liangjing, the perimeter patrol indeed proved lax.
translations.idiomatic: That year, when the emperor reached Liangjing, the security around him proved dangerously slack—as Boxiong had warned.

sentences.zh: 上思伯雄之言，及還，遷禮部尚書，謂近臣曰：「群臣有幹局者眾矣，如伯雄忠實，皆莫及也。」

translations.literal: The emperor recalled Boxiong's words. Upon his return he promoted him to Minister of Rites and said to his close ministers: "Among the ministers there are many capable administrators, but in loyalty and integrity like Boxiong's, none can match him.
translations.idiomatic: Remembering Boxiong's counsel, the emperor on his return made him minister of rites and told his inner circle, "Plenty of ministers know how to manage affairs, but for steadfast loyalty like Boxiong's, none can compare."

sentences.zh: 上謂伯雄曰：「龍逄、比干皆以忠諫而死，使遇明君，豈有是哉！」

translations.literal: The emperor said to Boxiong: "Long Feng and Bi Gan both died for loyal remonstrance. Had they met an enlightened ruler, how could that have happened!
translations.idiomatic: He said to Boxiong directly, "Long Feng and Bi Gan died for speaking truth to power. Under a clear-sighted ruler, would such men have to die?"

sentences.zh: 伯雄對曰：「魏徵願為良臣，正謂遇明君耳。」

translations.literal: Boxiong replied: "Wei Zheng wished to be a good minister precisely because he met an enlightened ruler.
translations.idiomatic: Boxiong answered, "Wei Zheng spoke of wanting to be a true minister—because he had found one."

sentences.zh: 因顧謂宰相曰：「《書》曰：'汝無面從，退有後言。

translations.literal: Then, turning to the chief ministers, he said: "The Documents says: 'Do not agree to my face and speak otherwise behind my back.
translations.idiomatic: Turning to his chief ministers, he quoted the Book of Documents: "Do not nod assent to my face and murmur against me afterward.

sentences.zh: '朕與卿等共治天下，事有可否，即當面陳。

translations.literal: I and you together govern all under Heaven. When matters admit or forbid approval, you should state them to my face at once.
translations.idiomatic: I and you govern this realm together. When something is right or wrong, say so to my face.

sentences.zh: 卿等致位卿相，正行道揚名之時，偷安自便，徼幸一時，如後世何？」

translations.literal: You have risen to the rank of ministers and chief ministers—this is precisely the time to walk the Way and make your names known. To seek ease for yourselves and grasp at momentary fortune—what will posterity think?'
translations.idiomatic: You stand at the height of power, the moment to serve honorably and leave a name. If you settle for comfort and chase quick advantage, what will history say of you?"

sentences.zh: 群臣皆稱萬歲。

translations.literal: The ministers all shouted "Long live [the emperor]!"
translations.idiomatic: The court cried "Long live the emperor!"

sentences.zh: 十二年，改沁南軍節度使，召為翰林學士承旨。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he was made military commissioner of the Qinnan Army, then summoned as Chief Hanlin Academician.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year he was appointed military commissioner of the Qinnan Army, then recalled to serve as chief Hanlin academician.

sentences.zh: 丞相石琚致仕，上問：「誰可代卿者？」

translations.literal: Chief Minister Shi Kui retired from office. The emperor asked: "Who can replace you?
translations.idiomatic: When Chief Minister Shi Kui retired, the emperor asked him, "Who can take your place?"

sentences.zh: 琚對曰：「伯雄可。」

translations.literal: Kui replied: "Boxiong will do.
translations.idiomatic: Shi answered, "Boxiong."

sentences.zh: 時論以琚舉得其人。

translations.literal: Contemporary opinion held that Kui's recommendation had found the right man.
translations.idiomatic: Opinion at the time agreed that Shi had named the right man.

sentences.zh: 複權詹事，伯雄知無不言，匡救弘多。

translations.literal: He was again appointed acting Grand Tutor. Boxiong spoke forthrightly on all he knew, and his corrections and rescues were many.
translations.idiomatic: He also served as acting grand tutor, speaking without reserve and offering steady corrective counsel.

sentences.zh: 後宮僚有詭隨者，人必稱楊詹事以愧之。

translations.literal: When among the palace staff there were those who were shifty and compliant, people would cite Grand Tutor Yang to shame them.
translations.idiomatic: When a palace official acted evasively, people would invoke Grand Tutor Yang to shame him.

sentences.zh: 除定武軍節度使，改平陽尹。

translations.literal: He was appointed military commissioner of the Dingwu Army and transferred to magistrate of Pingyang.
translations.idiomatic: He was made military commissioner of the Dingwu Army, then magistrate of Pingyang.

sentences.zh: 先是，張浩治平陽，有惠政，及伯雄為尹，百姓稱之，曰：「前有張，後有楊。」

translations.literal: Earlier Zhang Hao had governed Pingyang with benevolent policies. When Boxiong became magistrate, the common people praised them, saying: "First there was Zhang; afterward there was Yang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Hao had earlier governed Pingyang with real benevolence. When Boxiong took the post, the people said, "First there was Zhang—then there was Yang."

sentences.zh: 徙河中尹。

translations.literal: He was transferred to magistrate of Hezhong.
translations.idiomatic: He was later transferred to magistrate of Hezhong.

sentences.zh: 卒，年六十五。

translations.literal: He died at the age of sixty-five.
translations.idiomatic: He died at sixty-five.

sentences.zh: 諡莊獻。

translations.literal: His posthumous title was Zhuangxian.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously titled Zhuangxian ("Solemn and Offering").

sentences.zh: 弟伯傑、伯仁，族兄伯淵。

translations.literal: His younger brothers were Bojie and Boren; his clansman elder brother was Boyuan.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brothers were Bojie and Boren; his cousin was Boyuan.

sentences.zh: 族兄 伯淵

translations.literal: Clansman elder brother Boyuan
translations.idiomatic: Boyuan, a cousin of the clan

sentences.zh: 伯淵字宗之。

translations.literal: Boyuan's courtesy name was Zongzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Boyuan's style name was Zongzhi.

sentences.zh: 父丘文，遼中書舍人。

translations.literal: His father was Qiu Wen, Secretariat Drafter under the Liao.
translations.idiomatic: His father, Qiu Wen, had served the Liao as a secretariat drafter.

sentences.zh: 伯淵早孤，事母以孝聞，疏財好施，喜收古書。

translations.literal: Boyuan was orphaned early. He was known for filial service to his mother, was free with wealth and fond of giving, and delighted in collecting old books.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned young, Boyuan was known for devotion to his mother, for generosity with his money, and for collecting antique books.

sentences.zh: 天會初，以名家子補尚書省令史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianhui, as the son of a notable family he was appointed as clerk in the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Tianhui era he entered the Department of State Affairs as a clerk, benefiting from his family's standing.

sentences.zh: 十四年，賜進士第，曆吏、禮二部主事、御前承應文字，秩滿，除同知永定軍節度使事。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year he was granted jinshi standing, served successively as section chief in the Ministries of Personnel and Rites and as drafter before the throne, and when his term was complete was appointed vice military commissioner of the Yongding Army.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year he received jinshi rank, served as section chief in the ministries of personnel and rites and as imperial drafter, and at term's end was made deputy military commissioner of the Yongding Army.

sentences.zh: 召為司計郎中。

translations.literal: He was summoned as Director in the Department of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled to serve as director in the Department of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 知平定軍，用廉，遷平州路轉運使。

translations.literal: As administrator of the Pingding Army, for integrity he was promoted to transport commissioner of the Pingzhou Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: As administrator of the Pingding Army he won promotion to transport commissioner of Pingzhou Circuit on account of his integrity.

sentences.zh: 知泰安軍，有惠政，百姓刻石紀其事。

translations.literal: As administrator of the Tai'an Army he enacted benevolent policies, and the common people carved stone to record the affair.
translations.idiomatic: At Tai'an Army he governed with benevolence, and the people set up a stone inscription to record it.

sentences.zh: 四遷山東東路轉運使。

translations.literal: After four promotions he became transport commissioner of the Eastern Shandong Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: After four further promotions he became transport commissioner of Eastern Shandong Circuit.

sentences.zh: 正隆末，群盜蜂起，州郡往往罹害，獨濟南賴伯淵保全。

translations.literal: At the end of Zhenglong bandits rose everywhere like bees. Prefectures and districts often suffered harm; only Jinan, relying on Boyuan, was preserved intact.
translations.idiomatic: In the late Zhenglong era bandits swarmed across the land and prefectures fell one after another; only Jinan, under Boyuan's protection, remained secure.

sentences.zh: 大定三年，致仕，卒於家。

translations.literal: In the third year of Dading he retired from office and died at home.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Dading he retired and died at home.

sentences.zh: 蕭貢，字真卿，京兆咸陽人。

translations.literal: Xiao Gong, courtesy name Zhenqing, was a native of Xianyang in Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Gong, whose style name was Zhenqing, came from Xianyang in the Jingzhao region.

sentences.zh: 大定二十二年進士，調鎮戎州判官，涇陽令，涇州觀察判官。

translations.literal: A jinshi of the twenty-second year of Dading, he was appointed adjudicator of Zhenrongzhou, magistrate of Jingyang, and surveillance adjudicator of Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Placed on the jinshi rolls in the twenty-second year of Dading, he served successively as adjudicator at Zhenrong Prefecture, magistrate of Jingyang, and surveillance adjudicator at Jing Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 補尚書省令史。

translations.literal: He was appointed as clerk in the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed a clerk in the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 舊例，試補兩月，乃補用。

translations.literal: By old rule, after probationary appointment for two months one was formally appointed.
translations.idiomatic: By custom a clerk served a two-month probation before formal appointment.

sentences.zh: 貢至數日，執政以為能，即用之。

translations.literal: Gong had been there only several days when the chief ministers considered him capable and immediately appointed him.
translations.idiomatic: Gong had been there only a few days when the chief ministers, judging him capable, gave him a formal post at once.

sentences.zh: 擢監察御史。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Investigating Censor.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to investigating censor.

sentences.zh: 提刑司奏涇州有美政，遷北京轉運副使。

translations.literal: The Office of Circuit Intendant reported that Jingzhou had excellent governance, and he was promoted to Vice Transport Commissioner of the Northern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: When the circuit intendant's office reported exemplary governance at Jing, he was made vice transport commissioner of the Northern Capital.

sentences.zh: 親老，歸養。

translations.literal: His parents were aged; he returned home to support them.
translations.idiomatic: With elderly parents at home, he resigned to care for them.

sentences.zh: 左丞董師中、右丞楊伯通薦其文學，除翰林修撰。

translations.literal: Left Vice Director Dong Shizhong and Right Vice Director Yang Botong recommended his literary learning, and he was appointed Hanlin Compiler.
translations.idiomatic: Left Vice Director Dong Shizhong and Right Vice Director Yang Botong commended his scholarship, and he was made Hanlin compiler.

sentences.zh: 上書論：「比年之弊，人才不以器識、操履，巧於案牘，不涉吏議者為工。

translations.literal: He submitted a memorial discussing: "The recent abuses: talent is not judged by capacity, insight, and conduct; those skillful at documents who do not touch on administrative discussion are considered adept.
translations.idiomatic: In a memorial he wrote: "Among recent abuses is this: men are judged not by character or conduct but by paperwork—whoever handles documents cleverly without stirring administrative debate is called capable.

sentences.zh: 用人不務因才授官，惟泥資敘。

translations.literal: In employing men one does not strive to assign offices according to talent, but only clings to seniority in rank.
translations.idiomatic: Appointments follow seniority alone, not the fit between man and post.

sentences.zh: 名器不務慎與，人多僥倖。

translations.literal: Honorary titles and offices are not carefully bestowed; many people harbor opportunistic hopes.
translations.idiomatic: Honors are handed out without care, and opportunism spreads.

sentences.zh: 守令不務才實，民罹其害。

translations.literal: Prefects and magistrates do not strive for real talent; the people suffer their harm.
translations.idiomatic: Prefects and magistrates are chosen without regard to real ability, and the people pay the price.

sentences.zh: 伏望擢真才以振澆俗，核功能以理職業，慎名器以抑僥倖，重守令以厚邦本。

translations.literal: I humbly hope that true talent may be elevated to revive decadent custom, that functions may be examined to put duties in order, that honorary titles and offices may be carefully bestowed to suppress opportunism, and that prefects and magistrates may be valued to strengthen the foundation of the state.
translations.idiomatic: I pray Your Majesty will raise true talent to revive a corrupted age, weigh men by what they accomplish, guard honors jealously to curb opportunism, and choose local officials with care to strengthen the realm's foundation.

sentences.zh: 然後政化可行，百事可舉矣。」

translations.literal: Only then can government and transformation be carried out, and the hundred affairs be accomplished.
translations.idiomatic: Only then can policy take root and every undertaking succeed."

sentences.zh: 詔詞臣作《唐用董重質誅郭誼得失論》，貢為第一，賜重幣四端。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the literary officials to compose "An Essay on the Gains and Losses of Tang's Use of Dong Chongzhi to Execute Guo Yi." Gong ranked first and was granted four bolts of heavy silk.
translations.idiomatic: The court ordered the literati to write "On the Pros and Cons of Tang's Use of Dong Chongzhi to Execute Guo Yi." Gong's essay ranked first, and he received four bolts of fine silk.

sentences.zh: 貢論時政五弊，言路四難，詞意切至，改治書侍御史。

translations.literal: Gong discussed five abuses in current affairs and four difficulties on the path of remonstrance; his language was incisive. He was transferred to Supervising Censor of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: His discussion of five current abuses and four obstacles to candid speech was pointed and forceful; he was made supervising censor in the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 丁父憂，起複，改右司員外郎，尋轉郎中，遷國子祭酒，兼太常少卿，與陳大任刊修《遼史》。

translations.literal: When his father died he entered mourning, then was recalled from mourning and transferred to Vice Director in the Right Office, soon promoted to Director, then made Chancellor of the Directorate of Education, concurrently Vice Minister of Rites, and with Chen Daren edited the History of Liao.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning his father he was recalled to serve as vice director and then director in the right office, then as chancellor of the directorate of education and vice minister of rites, and he joined Chen Daren in editing the History of Liao.

sentences.zh: 改刑部侍郎，曆同知大興府事、德州防禦使，三遷河東北路按察轉運使。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Vice Minister of Punishments, served successively as Vice Administrator of Daxing Prefecture and defensive commissioner of Dezhou, and after three promotions became surveillance and transport commissioner of the Northeastern Hedong Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He became vice minister of punishments, served as deputy administrator of Daxing Prefecture and defensive commissioner of Dezhou, and after three promotions was made surveillance and transport commissioner of Northeastern Hedong Circuit.

sentences.zh: 大安末，改彰德軍節度事。

translations.literal: At the end of Da'an he was transferred to military commissioner of the Zhangde Army.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of the Da'an era he was made military commissioner of the Zhangde Army.

sentences.zh: 坐兵興不能守城，亡失百姓，降同知通遠軍節度使。

translations.literal: Because when war arose he could not hold the city and the common people were lost, he was demoted to vice military commissioner of the Tongyuan Army.
translations.idiomatic: When war broke out he failed to hold the city and lost the populace; he was demoted to deputy military commissioner of the Tongyuan Army.

sentences.zh: 未幾，改靜難軍節度使，曆河東北路、南京路轉運使、御史中丞，戶部尚書。

translations.literal: Before long he was transferred to military commissioner of the Jingnan Army, and served successively as transport commissioner of the Northeastern Hedong Circuit and the Nanjing Circuit, Censor-in-Chief, and Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made military commissioner of the Jingnan Army, then transport commissioner on the Northeastern Hedong and Nanjing circuits, censor-in-chief, and minister of revenue.

sentences.zh: 南京戒嚴，坐乏軍儲，詔釋不問。

translations.literal: When Nanjing was placed under martial law, he was charged with lack of military stores; an edict released him without inquiry.
translations.idiomatic: During Nanjing's military emergency he was faulted for inadequate grain stores, but an edict excused him from punishment.

sentences.zh: 興定元年，致仕。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xingding he retired from office.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Xingding he retired.

sentences.zh: 元光二年卒，諡文簡。

translations.literal: He died in the second year of Yuanguang and was posthumously titled Wenjian.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the second year of Yuanguang and was posthumously titled Wenjian ("Literary and Simple").

sentences.zh: 貢好學，讀書至老不倦，有注《史記》一百卷。

translations.literal: Gong loved learning and read books without weariness to old age. He had a commentary on the Records of the Grand Historian in one hundred scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: Gong loved learning and read without ceasing into old age; he left a hundred-scroll commentary on the Records of the Grand Historian.

sentences.zh: 溫蒂罕締達

translations.literal: Wendihandida
translations.idiomatic: Wendihandida

sentences.zh: 溫蒂罕締達，該習經史，以女直字出身，累官國史院編修官。

translations.literal: Wendihandida was thoroughly versed in the classics and histories. Starting from the Jurchen script examination, he rose through successive offices to compiler in the National History Institute.
translations.idiomatic: Wendihandida was deeply learned in the classics and histories. Having entered service through the Jurchen-script examination track, he rose to compiler at the National History Institute.

sentences.zh: 初，丞相希尹制女直字，設學校，使訛離剌等教之。

translations.literal: At first Chief Minister Xiyin devised the Jurchen script, established schools, and had Elila and others teach it.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Minister Xiyin had first devised the Jurchen script, opened schools, and assigned Elila and others to teach it.

sentences.zh: 其後學者漸盛，轉習經史，故納合椿年、紇石烈良弼皆由此致位宰相。

translations.literal: Afterward students gradually flourished and turned to studying the classics and histories. Hence Nahe Chunnian and Heshelie Liangbi both by this path reached the rank of chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: Students soon multiplied and moved on to the classics and histories—paths by which Nahe Chunnian and Heshelie Liangbi both reached the chancellorship.

sentences.zh: 締達最號精深。

translations.literal: Dida was most renowned for profound mastery.
translations.idiomatic: Of them all, Dida was considered the most deeply accomplished.

sentences.zh: 大定十二年，詔締達所教生員習作詩、策，若有文采，量才任使，其自願從學者聽。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year of Dading an edict ordered that the students taught by Dida practice composing poetry and policy essays; if they showed literary talent they were to be assigned office according to capacity, and those who wished to study on their own were permitted.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year of Dading an edict directed Dida's pupils to practice poetry and policy essays; those who showed literary talent were to be employed according to their abilities, and others who wished to join the study were allowed to do so.

sentences.zh: 十三年，設女直進士科。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year the Jurchen jinshi examination was established.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year the court established the Jurchen jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 是歲，徒單鎰等二十七人登第。

translations.literal: That year, Tushan Yi and twenty-six others passed the examination.
translations.idiomatic: That year Tushan Yi and twenty-six others placed on the examination rolls.

sentences.zh: 十五年，締達遷著作佐郎，與編修官宗璧、尚書省譯史阿魯、吏部令史張克忠譯解經書。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year Dida was transferred to Assistant Gentleman at the Office of Drafting and, with Compiler Zong Bi, Translator Aru of the Department of State Affairs, and Clerical Officer Zhang Kezhong of the Ministry of Personnel, translated and explicated the classics.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year Dida was promoted to assistant gentleman at the Office of Drafting and, together with compiler Zong Bi, Department of State Affairs translator Aru, and Ministry of Personnel clerk Zhang Kezhong, worked on translating and annotating the classics.

sentences.zh: 累遷秘書丞。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted and became Deputy Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through successive appointments to deputy secretary.

sentences.zh: 十九年，改左贊善，以母老求養。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year he was reassigned as Left Mentor and, because his mother was elderly, requested leave to support her.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year he was made Left Mentor but asked to leave office to care for his aged mother.

sentences.zh: 顯宗使內直丞六斤謂締達曰：「贊善，初未除此官，天子謂孤曰：'朕得一出倫之才，學問該貫，當令輔汝德義。

translations.literal: Prince Xianzong sent Inner Attendant Director Liujin to tell Dida: "Left Mentor, at first this office had not yet been conferred on you. The Son of Heaven said to me, 'I have obtained a talent of surpassing excellence, thoroughly versed in learning; he should assist you in virtue and righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Xianzong sent Inner Attendant Director Liujin to tell Dida: "Left Mentor—when this post was first discussed, it had not yet been conferred on you. The Son of Heaven told me, 'I have found an extraordinary talent, comprehensively learned; he should guide you in virtue and righteousness.

sentences.zh: '既數日，贊善除此官。

translations.literal: A few days later the Left Mentor was given this office.
translations.idiomatic: Within days the Left Mentor received the appointment.

sentences.zh: 自謂親炙德義，不勝其喜。

translations.literal: I myself expect to be personally warmed by virtue and righteousness and cannot contain my delight.
translations.idiomatic: I shall be warmed at close hand by virtue and righteousness—my joy is beyond measure.

sentences.zh: 未可去也，勿難於懷。」

translations.literal: You must not leave yet; do not let it weigh on your heart."
translations.idiomatic: You cannot go yet; do not burden your heart with this."

sentences.zh: 久之，轉翰林待制，卒。

translations.literal: After a long time he was transferred to Hanlin Attendant-in-Waiting and died.
translations.idiomatic: In time he was made Hanlin attendant-in-waiting and later died.

sentences.zh: 明昌五年，贈翰林學士承旨，諡文成。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Mingchang he was posthumously granted Chief Attending Scholar of the Hanlin Academy and honored with the posthumous name Wencheng.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Mingchang he was posthumously made chief attending scholar of the Hanlin Academy, with the posthumous title Wencheng.

sentences.zh: 子二十，章宗即位，以為符寶典書，累官左諫議大夫。

translations.literal: His son Ershi, when Emperor Zhangzong acceded, was appointed Keeper of Seals and Treasures and rose through successive offices to Left Remonstrating Grand Master.
translations.idiomatic: His son Ershi entered service when Zhangzong took the throne as keeper of seals and treasures and rose to left remonstrating grand master.

sentences.zh: 貞祐四年，上疏，略曰：「今邊備未撤，徵調不休，州縣長吏不知愛養其民，督責征科，鞭笞逼迫，急於星火，文移重複，不勝其弊，宜敕有司務從簡易。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Zhenyou he submitted a memorial, the gist of which read: "Border defenses have not yet been withdrawn and levies never cease. Prefectural and county chief officials do not know how to cherish and nurture their people; they press tax collection, lash and drive them, urgent as shooting stars; documents and orders repeat endlessly—the abuses are unbearable. The responsible offices should be ordered to strive for simplicity.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Zhenyou he memorialized the throne, writing in part: "With frontier garrisons still unmustered and exactions unending, local magistrates no longer cherish the people they rule. They hound them for taxes, whip and drive them with fire-alarm urgency, and bury them under duplicate orders—the harm is intolerable. Command the responsible offices to simplify their ways.

sentences.zh: 兵興以來，忠臣烈士，孝子順孫，義夫節婦，湮沒無聞者甚眾，乞遣史官一員，廣為採訪，以議褒嘉。」

translations.literal: Since war began, loyal ministers, martyrs, filial sons, obedient grandsons, righteous husbands, and chaste wives who have sunk into obscurity are very numerous. I beg that one historiographer be dispatched to gather accounts widely, so that rewards and honors may be deliberated."
translations.idiomatic: Since the wars began, countless worthy souls—loyal ministers, martyrs, filial sons, dutiful grandsons, faithful husbands, and chaste wives—have vanished without renown. Send a historiographer to seek their stories widely, so the court may decide how to honor them."

sentences.zh: 興定元年，遷武勝軍節度使，改吏部尚書，知開封府。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xingding he was transferred to military governor of the Wusheng Army, changed to Minister of Personnel, and served as prefect of Kaifeng.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Xingding he became military governor of the Wusheng Army, then minister of personnel and prefect of Kaifeng.

sentences.zh: 坐縱軍人家屬出城，當杖，詔解職。

translations.literal: He was liable for allowing soldiers' families to leave the city and should have been beaten with the staff; an edict relieved him of office.
translations.idiomatic: For permitting soldiers' families to leave the city he was liable to beating with the staff; an edict stripped him of office.

sentences.zh: 四年，複知開封府，複坐以事囑警巡使完顏金僧奴，降為鄭州防禦使。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he again served as prefect of Kaifeng and again, for asking Patrol Commissioner Wanyan Jinsengnu to handle a matter on his behalf, was demoted to defender of Zheng Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he was again prefect of Kaifeng, but once more—for pressing Patrol Commissioner Wanyan Jinsengnu to take up a personal matter—was demoted to defender of Zheng Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 未幾，複為知開封府事。

translations.literal: Before long he again became Administrator of Kaifeng.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was reappointed administrator of Kaifeng.

sentences.zh: 張翰，字林卿，忻州秀容人。

translations.literal: Zhang Han, courtesy name Linqing, was a native of Xiurong in Xin Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Han, style name Linqing, came from Xiurong in Xin Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 大定二十八年進士，調隰州軍事判官。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination in the twenty-eighth year of Dading and was assigned as military affairs adjudicator of Xi Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: After placing on the jinshi rolls in the twenty-eighth year of Dading, he was posted as military affairs adjudicator of Xi Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 有誣昆弟三人為劫者，翰微行廉得其狀，白於州釋之。

translations.literal: When three brothers were falsely accused as robbers, Han made discreet inquiries, thoroughly ascertained the facts, reported to the prefecture, and had them released.
translations.idiomatic: When three brothers were falsely charged as bandits, Han investigated in secret, learned the truth, and persuaded the prefecture to release them.

sentences.zh: 曆東勝、義豐、會川令，補尚書省令史，除戶部主事，遷監察御史。

translations.literal: He served successively as magistrate of Dongsheng, Yifeng, and Huichuan, was appointed clerk in the Department of State Affairs, was made Director in the Ministry of Revenue, and was promoted to Investigating Censor.
translations.idiomatic: He served as magistrate of Dongsheng, Yifeng, and Huichuan in turn, entered the Department of State Affairs as a clerk, was appointed director in the Ministry of Revenue, and rose to investigating censor.

sentences.zh: 丁母憂，服闋，調山東路鹽使。

translations.literal: When his mother died he entered mourning; when the mourning period ended he was assigned as salt commissioner of the Eastern Shandong Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning his mother he was posted as salt commissioner of the Eastern Shandong Circuit.

sentences.zh: 丁父憂，起複尚書省都事、戶部員外郎。

translations.literal: When his father died he was recalled from mourning and made Director in the Department of State Affairs and Vice Director in the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: Called back from mourning after his father's death, he was made department director and vice director in the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 大安間，平章政事獨吉思忠、參知政事承裕行省戍邊，翰充左右司郎中，論議不相協。

translations.literal: During the Da'an period Grand Councillor Dujishi Zhong and Vice Grand Councillor Chengyu held a provincial commission guarding the frontier; Han served as Director in the Left and Right Departments, and their deliberations did not agree.
translations.idiomatic: In the Da'an era, as Grand Councillor Dujishi Zhong and Vice Grand Councillor Chengyu held a frontier provincial commission, Han served as director in the left and right departments, but their counsels did not align.

sentences.zh: 處置乖方，翰屢爭之不見省。

translations.literal: Measures were ill-suited; Han repeatedly remonstrated but was not heeded.
translations.idiomatic: Policy went awry, and though Han protested again and again, his views were ignored.

sentences.zh: 承裕就逮，衛紹王知翰嘗有言，召見撫慰之。

translations.literal: When Chengyu was arrested, Emperor Weishao knew Han had once spoken out, summoned him, and comforted him.
translations.idiomatic: After Chengyu was taken into custody, Emperor Weishao, knowing Han had spoken up, summoned and reassured him.

sentences.zh: 改知登聞鼓院，兼前職，遷侍御史。

translations.literal: He was changed to Administrator of the Hall for Striking the Drum of Grievances, concurrently keeping his former post, and was promoted to Attending Censor.
translations.idiomatic: He was made administrator of the Hall for Striking the Drum of Grievances while retaining his prior duties, then promoted to attending censor.

sentences.zh: 貞祐初，為翰林直學士，充元帥府經歷官。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhenyou he was Direct Academician of the Hanlin Academy and served as administrative officer of the Field Marshal's headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Zhenyou he became Hanlin direct academician and administrative officer on the field marshal's staff.

sentences.zh: 中都戒嚴，調度方殷，改戶部侍郎。

translations.literal: With martial law in the Central Capital and supplies urgently needed, he was changed to Vice Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: As the Central Capital came under martial law and logistics grew urgent, he was made vice minister of revenue.

sentences.zh: 宣宗遷汴，翰規措扈從糧草至真定，上書言五事：「一曰強本。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xuanzong moved the court to Bian, Han organized escort provisions as far as Zhending and submitted a memorial setting forth five points: "First, strengthen the root.
translations.idiomatic: When Xuanzong relocated to Bian, Han arranged provisions for the imperial entourage as far as Zhending and memorialized five proposals: "First, strengthen the foundation.

sentences.zh: 謂當裒兵徒、徙豪民，以實南京。

translations.literal: This means gathering troops and settlers and moving powerful families to fill out the Southern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: Gather troops and colonists and relocate prominent households to bolster the Southern Capital.

sentences.zh: 二曰足用。

translations.literal: Second, ensure sufficiency.
translations.idiomatic: Second, secure adequate supply.

sentences.zh: 謂當按蔡、汴舊渠以通漕運。

translations.literal: This means reopening the old canals of Cai and Bian to restore grain transport.
translations.idiomatic: Clear and restore the old Cai and Bian canals to reopen grain transport.

sentences.zh: 三曰防亂。

translations.literal: Third, guard against disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Third, guard against unrest.

sentences.zh: 謂當就集義軍假之官印，使相統攝，以安反側。

translations.literal: This means organizing the Jiyi Army locally, lending them official seals, and having them command one another to settle the unsettled.
translations.idiomatic: Organize the Jiyi Army on the spot, lend them official seals, and let them command one another to pacify wavering elements.

sentences.zh: 四曰省事。

translations.literal: Fourth, simplify administration.
translations.idiomatic: Fourth, simplify government.

sentences.zh: 謂縣邑不能自立者宜稍並之，既以省官，且易於備盜。

translations.literal: This means that counties and districts unable to sustain themselves should be slightly merged—both to reduce officials and to make guarding against bandits easier.
translations.idiomatic: Merge counties too weak to stand alone—fewer officials, and bandits easier to suppress.

sentences.zh: 五曰推恩。

translations.literal: Fifth, extend grace.
translations.idiomatic: Fifth, extend imperial grace.

sentences.zh: 謂當推恩以示天子所在稱幸之意。」

translations.literal: This means extending grace to show that wherever the Son of Heaven is present is called a place of imperial favor."
translations.idiomatic: Bestow favors to show that wherever the Son of Heaven tarries should be honored as a place of his gracious presence."

sentences.zh: 上略施行之。

translations.literal: The Emperor largely implemented them.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor adopted most of these measures.

sentences.zh: 翰雅有治劇才，所至輒辦。

translations.literal: Han naturally had talent for handling difficult affairs and wherever he went accomplished them at once.
translations.idiomatic: Han had a gift for hard administration and finished whatever he took in hand.

sentences.zh: 遷河平軍節度使、都水監、提控軍馬使，俄改戶部尚書。

translations.literal: He was promoted to military governor of the Heping Army, Director of Waterways, Commissioner Controlling Military Horses, and soon changed to Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to military governor of the Heping Army, director of waterways, and commissioner controlling military horses, then soon became minister of revenue.

sentences.zh: 是時，初至南京，庶事草略，翰經度區處，皆有條理。

translations.literal: At that time, having just arrived at the Southern Capital, affairs were still in rough outline; Han planned and arranged them all with order.
translations.idiomatic: The court had only just reached the Southern Capital and everything was still improvised; Han organized it all with clear method.

sentences.zh: 是歲卒，諡達義。

translations.literal: That year he died and was posthumously titled Dayi.
translations.idiomatic: He died that year and received the posthumous name Dayi.

sentences.zh: 任天寵

translations.literal: Ren Tianchong
translations.idiomatic: Ren Tianchong

sentences.zh: 任天寵，字清叔，曹州定陶人也，明昌二年進士，調考城主簿，再遷威戎縣令。

translations.literal: Ren Tianchong, courtesy name Qingshu, was a native of Dingtao in Cao Prefecture. He passed the jinshi examination in the second year of Mingchang, was assigned as chief clerk of Kaocheng, and was twice promoted to magistrate of Weirong County.
translations.idiomatic: Ren Tianchong, style name Qingshu, came from Dingtao in Cao Prefecture. He took the jinshi in the second year of Mingchang, served as chief clerk of Kaocheng, and rose twice to magistrate of Weirong County.

sentences.zh: 縣故堡寨，無文廟學舍，天寵以廢署建。

translations.literal: The county had formerly been a fortified settlement and had no Confucian temple or school; Tianchong built them in an abandoned government office.
translations.idiomatic: The county was once a fortified outpost without temple or school; Tianchong built both in a disused yamen.

sentences.zh: 有兄弟訟田者，天寵諭以理義，委曲周至，皆感泣而去。

translations.literal: When brothers sued one another over fields, Tianchong instructed them in principle and duty with thorough tact; all wept and departed.
translations.idiomatic: When brothers came to court over land, Tianchong reasoned with them gently and thoroughly until both left in tears.

sentences.zh: 調泰定軍節度判官。

translations.literal: He was assigned as military commissioner's adjudicator of the Taiding Army.
translations.idiomatic: He was posted as military commissioner's adjudicator of the Taiding Army.

sentences.zh: 丁父憂，服闋，調崇義軍節度判官。

translations.literal: When his father died he entered mourning; when the mourning period ended he was assigned as military commissioner's adjudicator of the Chongyi Army.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning his father he was assigned as military commissioner's adjudicator of the Chongyi Army.

sentences.zh: 補尚書省令史、右三部檢法司正，遷監察御史。

translations.literal: He was appointed clerk in the Department of State Affairs and Director of the Inspection Law Bureau of the Three Right Departments and was promoted to Investigating Censor.
translations.idiomatic: He entered the Department of State Affairs as a clerk and director of the inspection law bureau of the three right departments, then rose to investigating censor.

sentences.zh: 改右司都事，遷員外郎。

translations.literal: He was changed to Director in the Right Department and promoted to Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: He moved to director in the right department and then to vice director.

sentences.zh: 改左司諫，轉左司郎中，遷國子祭酒。

translations.literal: He was changed to Left Remonstrator, transferred to Director in the Left Department, and promoted to Chancellor of the National University.
translations.idiomatic: He became left remonstrator, then director in the left department, and finally chancellor of the National University.

sentences.zh: 貞祐初，轉秘書監兼吏部侍郎，改中都路都轉運使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhenyou he was transferred to Secretary Supervisor and concurrent Vice Minister of Personnel and was changed to transport commissioner of the Central Capital Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Zhenyou he became secretary supervisor and concurrent vice minister of personnel, then transport commissioner of the Central Capital Circuit.

sentences.zh: 時京師戒嚴，糧運艱阻，天寵悉力營辦，曲盡勞瘁，出家貲以濟饑者，全活甚眾。

translations.literal: At that time the capital was under martial law and grain transport was difficult and obstructed; Tianchong exerted all his strength in provision, exhausting every effort, and spent from personal wealth to aid the hungry—very many were kept alive.
translations.idiomatic: With the capital under martial law and grain routes blocked, Tianchong strained every nerve to supply it, spending his own fortune to feed the hungry and saving countless lives.

sentences.zh: 監察御史高夔、劉元規舉天寵二十人公勤明敏，有材幹，可安集百姓。

translations.literal: Investigating Censors Gao Kui and Liu Yuangui recommended Tianchong as diligent in public service, perceptive and capable, able to settle and gather the people.
translations.idiomatic: Censors Gao Kui and Liu Yuangui recommended Tianchong, praising his public diligence, sharp intelligence, and capacity to settle and reassure the people.

sentences.zh: 遷戶部尚書。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He was made minister of revenue.

sentences.zh: 三年，中都不守，天寵繼走南京，中道遇兵，死之。

translations.literal: In the third year the Central Capital was lost; Tianchong fled in turn to the Southern Capital and, on the road, encountered soldiers and died.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year, when the Central Capital fell, Tianchong fled toward the Southern Capital and was killed by soldiers on the way.

sentences.zh: 諡純肅。

translations.literal: He was posthumously titled Chundu.
translations.idiomatic: He received the posthumous title Chundu.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：程寀、任熊祥，遼之進士，孔璠、范拱事宋、事齊，太祖皆見禮遇，而金之文治日以盛矣。

translations.literal: The encomium reads: Cheng Cai and Ren Xiongxiang were jinshi of the Liao; Kong Fan and Fan Gong served the Song and then the Qi. Taizu treated them all with courtesy and respect, and thus the literary governance of the Jin grew daily in splendor.
translations.idiomatic: The encomium says: Cheng Cai and Ren Xiongxiang were Liao jinshi; Kong Fan and Fan Gong served Song and Qi in turn. Taizu honored them all, and from that hour Jin letters flourished.

sentences.zh: 張用直，海陵父子並列舊學。

translations.literal: Zhang Yongzhi taught both Hailing and his son in the old learning.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yongzhi numbered both Hailing and his son among his pupils in the old learning.

sentences.zh: 劉樞之練達，王翛之強敏于事，楊伯雄之善諷諫、工辭藻，蕭貢、溫蒂罕締達之文藝適時，之數人者迭用於正隆、大定、明昌之間。

translations.literal: Liu Shu's seasoned competence, Wang Xiao's forceful responsiveness in affairs, Yang Boxiong's skill in gentle remonstrance and literary ornament, and the timely literary attainments of Xiao Gong and Wendihandida—these several men were employed in succession during the Zhenglong, Dading, and Mingchang periods.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Shu brought seasoned judgment; Wang Xiao, force and speed in office; Yang Boxiong, remonstrance raised to art and a polished pen; Xiao Gong and Wendihandida, letters fitted to their age—these men served in turn through Zhenglong, Dading, and Mingchang.

sentences.zh: 張翰、任天寵之經理調度，宣宗南遷，猶賴其用焉。

translations.literal: In the management and coordination of Zhang Han and Ren Tianchong, when Emperor Xuanzong moved south, the court still relied on their use.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Han and Ren Tianchong supplied the logistics and planning on which Xuanzong still depended after the southern move.

sentences.zh: 金源氏百餘年所以培植人才而獲其效者，於斯可概見矣。

translations.literal: How the Jinyuan clan for more than a hundred years cultivated talent and reaped its fruits may be broadly seen from this.
translations.idiomatic: In these lives one may glimpse how the house of Jin, across more than a century, cultivated men of talent—and what that cultivation yielded.
